Brief Posting Description

The M FU EMERGENCY PLANNING & PREPAREDNESS Department of the P EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS & RESPONSE Division at Hawaiian Electric Company has 1 Management vacancy available. (Role: Professional)

Job Function

Works under the direction of the Manager, EPP as the onsite Subject Matter Expert for emergency management and incident response. Leads IMT efforts as the on-site Incident Advisor. Manages the development, planning, and execution of the Company’s Emergency Planning and Preparedness (EPP) policies and plans, including the Electrical Service Restoration Plan (ESRP) and Emergency Action Plans for their assigned location ensuring alignment across the Company. Drives collaborative team efforts to assess and address risks of the Company’s emergency management plans. Drives work prioritzation efforts and manages assigned work plan and implementation across all areas.

Essential Functions

Manages the functions and activities of the EPP programs and IMT working group across the company ensuring all programs are maintained, metrics developed and recorded and reported as necessary.
Identifies and implements best practices and procedures for program maintenance; develops justification for projects supporting department programs including program budget planning & forecasting requirements. Supports real-world emergencies, serves as Incident Advisor to lead and support the Incident Management Teams.
Develops short term goals for department and manages the respective projects and processes in support of both short and long-term Company goals. Sets priorities, drives process improvement, and develops strategies and implementation plans to strengthen the organization’s emergency response infrastructure and program. Leads collaboration effort with internal stakeholders to ensure alignment across the Company. Resolves challenging and complex issues and escalates when necessary.
Drives the Company’s incident management response capabilities through a comprehensive training program that is enhanced with planning, drills, and exercises, incorporating industry best practices and lessons learned.
Delivers National Incident Management (NIMS) training as it relates to ESRP. Achieves measurable results in the training to response team members, and field and support staff as required.
Directs and coordinates with all sections to develop and schedule tabletops exercises and drills. Serves as point of contact for various internal and external stakeholders who are participating in the exercises and drills. Ensures post-training follow up actions and tasks are completed and implemented.
Manages the Learning Management System (LMS) and Enable Now in collaboration with Company stakeholders to optimize the learning experience, set up and assign courses, and maintaining and tracking training records.
Initiates and maintains liaisons with government agencies and emergency management stakeholders at the local, state, and Federal level, including electrical utility industry professionals, to facilitate emergency response plan development, coordination and execution.
Represents the Company on various Federal, State, County, community, and business emergency response committees. Stays current on government emergency response programs and policies.
Identifies inconsistencies in Company EPP processes and procedures when compared to government agency policies. Attends training programs to ensure Company is compliant with NIMS IMT standards. Creates and provides educational presentations to communities on emergency preparedness and distributes information regarding emergency preparedness and response procedures. Monitors changes in federal, state, and local laws and requirements related to emergency preparedness. Evaluates and proposes recommendations, and implementation of policy and program changes to respond to changing requirements. Works with internal and external stakeholders to achieve organizational goals.
Represents Hawaiian Electric at regional and National conferences / workshops, such as the Western Region Mutual Assistance Group conferences, Transmission & Distribution, Meter, & Mutual Assistance conferences, and other emergency management events.
Creates, maintains, and updates the EPP SharePoint sites as needed; oversees invoice approvals and tracking to budgeted line items. Develops and maintains budget. Develops and manages rate case communications and maintains datasets for PBR Reporting.
Provides general administrative duties in support of the EPP Department and performs other incidental duties as required and assigned. Subject to recall around the clock for emergency management operations, which may require irregular work hours, work at locations other than the official duty station and may include duties other than those specified in the official position description.
Participates in Company emergency response activities as assigned, including any activities required to prepare for such emergency response.

Basic Qualifications

Knowledge Requirements

A bachelor’s degree or a professional certification in emergency or disaster management, emergency preparedness, planning, homeland security, or a closely related field is preferred.
Demonstrated experience leading cross functional teams in building consensus.
Demonstrated experience in developing initiatives that introduce cross organizational change.
Demonstrated experience analyzing difficult issues involving the substantive nature of emergency management programs.
Demonstrated experience of project and program management principles, project/program management training and/or equivalent experience.
Demonstrated effective resource and project planning experience, decision making and results delivery.
Experience leading complex projects with multiple partners.
Knowledge of processes, concepts, and framework related to emergency management (National Incident Management System - NIMS).
Demonstrated experience and knowledge of general principles and practices of emergency management, emergency action plans.
Knowledge of, or willing to learn, SafeStart principles and best practices to achieve a safe workplace environment.
Must have or be able to obtain the Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program (HSEEP) Certification within 6 months.

Ability to remain flexible in a demanding work environment and adapt to rapidly changing priorities and strategic direction.
Ability to create and interpret trends, models, forecasts, and simulations.
Ability to interpret and apply Federal, state, and local laws, regulations, policies and standards regarding emergency management and response.
Strong written, oral, and listening communication skills and ability to articulate ideas and concepts clearly and concisely.

Advanced understanding of personal computer software applications such as Microsoft Office, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, Visio, Power BI, and Project Management software tools. Demonstrated expertise or aptitude for enterprise applications such as ERP/EAM and Sharepoint.
Ability to use communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills to resolve conflicts between parties.

Ability to plan, prioritize, schedule, and manage time and work to complete tasks and meet deadlines, while handling multiple assignments and remaining flexible and adapting to changing priorities.

Firestone Airide, specializes in air spring manufacturing and technology with a history of more than 80 years of research and development on technologically advanced air springs for the global marketplace. Firestone engineers air springs and related products for commercial trucks and trailers, cars, sport utility vehicles, light trucks, mini vans, motor homes, buses, agricultural equipment, rail and industrial applications.

Job Category

General Management

Position Summary

The Program Manager leads and coordinates the successful development and launch of automotive vehicle programs for Firestone Airide products. The project management role plans, organizes, and controls resources, procedures, budgets, and timing across complex, interrelated programs.

Serving as the primary liaison between customers, leadership, and internal cross-functional teams, the Program Manager ensures program objectives are achieved on time, within budget, and in compliance with customer, quality, performance, and profitability requirements.

The role manages programs from business case development and product development through launch, production, and post-launch support.

Responsibilities

Program and Project Leadership

Lead multiple automotive vehicle programs or complex business processes from concept through production launch and post-launch support (PDP process).
Organize cross-functional project teams, assign responsibilities, develop integrated schedules and milestones, and determine resource requirements.
Develop and maintain program plans, budgets, staffing assumptions, deliverables, dependencies, and governance routines.
Serve as the primary point of contact for customers and leadership regarding program status, risks, escalations, and key decisions.
Monitor and report project performance, including cost, timing, quality, profitability, and launch readiness.
Identify and resolve obstacles that could prevent completion on time, within budget, or in accordance with customer expectations.
Integrate supplier and vendor activities into the program plan, and track and review vendor deliverables when applicable.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Stakeholder Management

Coordinate activities across Product Engineering, Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain, Finance, Sales, Account Management, Customer Service, and customer teams.
Facilitate program reviews, launch readiness reviews, working sessions, and decision-making meetings.
Align internal and external stakeholders on priorities, deliverables, ownership, timing, and resource needs.
Build and sustain effective stakeholder relationships through clear communication, influence, negotiation, and timely issue resolution.
Drive accountability across functions, including teams not under the Program Manager's direct authority.

Product Development and Launch Execution

Manage product development milestones in accordance with customer requirements and internal processes.
Lead or support APQP activities and automotive launch processes, including PPAP readiness, FMEA, Control Plans, and related deliverables.
Coordinate change management throughout the program lifecycle, including scope, design, timing, cost, and customer changes.

Financial and Business Management

Track program financial performance against approved business cases and profitability targets.
Monitor tooling, development, and launch expenditures (CAPEX and OPEX).
Partner with Finance and functional teams on forecasting, budget management, cost optimization, and profitability improvement initiatives.
Evaluate financial risks and opportunities, support fact-based trade-off decisions, and communicate impacts to leadership.

Risk, Quality, and Compliance

Lead program risk assessments, mitigation plans, contingency planning, and escalation processes.
Ensure adherence to internal and external quality standards.
Drive corrective actions for issues affecting quality, delivery, cost, timing, or customer commitments.
Capture lessons learned and ensure improvements are incorporated into future programs and standard work.

Continuous Improvement and Executive Reporting

Identify continuous improvement and automation opportunities, conduct detailed analyses, and recommend actions that improve program execution and business performance.
Adapt established practices and, when appropriate, improve standard operating procedures to develop effective new solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent project management credential.
MBA, advanced technical degree, or relevant postgraduate education.
Automotive industry experience.
Knowledge of APQP, PPAP, FMEA, Control Plans, and automotive launch processes (not mandatory).
Experience working directly with OEM customers and Tier 1 suppliers.

Microsoft Project
Microsoft 365 applications
Power BI
SAP

Project scheduling, resource planning, and executive reporting

perception

and/or Navy applications

Familiarity with traditional DoW contractual structures such as cost plus fixed fee (CPFF), firm fixed price (FFP), and time and materials (T&M).

Experience managing engineering projects including driving schedule and budget.

Advanced degree (Masters/PhD) in relevant field (e.g., computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, business management or other related field) and 2+ years of relevant experience.

Continuous improvement mindset; identifies gaps and drives enhancements to delivery practices.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Project Manager to lead the planning, execution, and successful delivery of strategic IT initiatives. In this role, you will collaborate with business and IT stakeholders to translate business objectives into actionable project plans, manage project scope, timelines, risks, and dependencies, and ensure successful delivery of solutions that create measurable business value.

Planning: Defining the project's scope, goals, and objectives.
Budgeting: Estimating costs, establishing budgets, and tracking spending.

Issue resolution: Ensuring issues related to scope, budget, and resource allocation are resolved effectively.

Change management: Dealing with changes to the project, committed delivery on time with quality and ensuring zero impact to production due to changes.
Documentation: Preparing documents and managing reports.

10+ years of project management experience, including sustained leadership of large scale, complex IT enabled change initiatives.
Demonstrated track record of delivering large scale projects with material business impact, not only technical implementation.
Proven experience managing senior stakeholders, including influencing, negotiation and conflict resolution.
Strong leadership capability, including leading project managers, workstream leads and matrix teams in a multicultural, global environment.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands on delivery execution.
Strong commercial and financial acumen.

本ポジションでは、防衛省を含む政府機関および防衛関連企業に対し、生成AIを活用したサイバーセキュリティ事業の営業推進とプロジェクトマネジメントを担っていただきます。脆弱性診断やペネトレーションテストといったオフェンシブセキュリティの知見と、防御・運用側の課題を捉えるディフェンシブセキュリティの理解を併せ持ち、セキュリティエンジニアやAIリサーチャーと対等に議論しながら、提案から実行までをEnd-to-Endで牽引していただきます。
本ポジションはフルタイム、勤務地は日本となり、ビジネスレベル以上の日本語能力（N1目安）があることが求められます（ビジネスレベルの英語力があれば尚可）。

役割と責任

防衛分野のサイバーセキュリティにおける困難な課題を、アカウントマネージャー、エンジニア、AIリサーチャーと協働しながら特定し、AIを活用したソリューションとして提案・実行する
防衛省を含む政府機関および防衛関連企業との強固な関係を構築・維持し、新たなビジネスチャンスを開拓する
諸外国における防衛・サイバーセキュリティ分野の技術動向を踏まえた提案戦略を策定し、「そもそも何をどう作るか」からリードする
クライアントとの要件調整、期待値調整、課題整理を主導する
プロジェクト全体の品質・コスト・スケジュールに責任を持ち、確実なデリバリーを完遂する
開発チームのメンバーや技術パートナーと円滑なコミュニケーションを取り、プロジェクトのゴールに向けてチームを牽引・サポートする

応募資格およびスキル（Must）

サイバーセキュリティまたは防衛分野での5年以上の実務経験があり、以下のいずれかを想定
(i) 経営コンサルティングファームやシンクタンクにおいて、防衛省を含む政府機関のサイバーセキュリティ関連プロジェクトを主導した経験
(ii) セキュリティ専業企業において、脆弱性診断・ペネトレーションテスト等のサービス提供やその営業・デリバリーに携わった経験
(iii) 防衛分野のメーカーや商社において、防衛関連の政府機関向けに営業・プロジェクト推進を担当した経験
サイバーセキュリティの全体像に関する体系的な知見。特に、脆弱性診断やペネトレーションテストとは何か、セキュリティエンジニアが実務で何を行っているかを理解し、専門ベンダーのエンジニアと技術的な会話ができること。
エンタープライズまたは政府機関向けプロジェクトにおけるプロジェクトマネジメントの実務経験（ソフトウェア開発プロジェクトに限らない）。チームビルディング、タスク・課題管理、スケジュール管理、品質管理を自律的に遂行できること。
クライアントとの要件調整、期待値調整、課題整理を含む深い折衝経験と、要件定義書・計画書・課題管理表などのハイクオリティなドキュメンテーション能力があること。
生成AIやデータ基盤に関する基本的な仕組みの理解（API利用、モデル特性、データ前提、コスト・セキュリティ観点など）と、最新トレンドに自らキャッチアップする姿勢

歓迎要件（Nice to Have）

防衛分野・政府調達における法令・規制、ガイドラインの把握（防衛産業サイバーセキュリティ基準、装備品等の調達に係る秘密保全対策ガイドライン、防衛産業保全マニュアル、防衛事業適合事業者制度、ISMAP、NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171 等）
要件定義、技術選定、アーキテクチャ設計等の上流工程や、PoC・技術検証フェーズを含むプロジェクトの推進経験
生成AI（AIエージェント、Embedding、RAG等）を活用したシステムの要件整理・設計・リスク管理の経験
開発プロジェクトのチームマネジメントやメンバー育成の経験、およびPMP・Scrum Master・情報処理安全確保支援士・CISSP等の関連資格

At Sakana AI, we conduct world-leading research and development in unique generative AI technologies inspired by nature. We are now bringing the results of this research into the domain that protects society’s most critical foundations: cybersecurity.
In this position, you will drive business development and project management for our generative AI-powered cybersecurity business, serving major enterprises including financial institutions. Engaging with security engineers and AI researchers as an equal, you will lead engagements end-to-end, from proposal to execution.

Identify customers’ most difficult cybersecurity challenges in collaboration with account managers, engineers, and AI researchers, and propose and execute AI-powered solutions.

Lead requirements coordination, expectation management, and issue structuring with clients, and drive the strategy of what to build and how to build it.
Take ownership of quality, cost, and schedule across the entire project and ensure reliable delivery.
Communicate closely with development team members and technology partners, leading and supporting the team toward project goals.

(i) Experience leading cybersecurity projects at a management consulting firm or think tank.
(ii) Experience delivering, selling, or managing services such as vulnerability assessment and penetration testing at a cybersecurity company.
(iii) Experience leading the planning and execution of security initiatives in the security division of a financial institution or enterprise.

Systematic knowledge of the overall cybersecurity landscape. In particular, a solid understanding of what vulnerability assessments and penetration tests are and what security engineers do in practice, with the ability to hold technical conversations with engineers at specialized security vendors.

jobs.title: Technical Project Manager
jobs.description:
Harbor IT is a leading Managed Service Provider (MSP) specializing in delivering cutting edge Cybersecurity, IT, and Cloud Services to a diverse portfolio of clients. We pride ourselves on our commitment to excellence, innovation, and customer satisfaction. Harbor IT is backed by investment firm Worklyn Partners since 2022 and has built a national platform through acquisition and rapid organic growth. Our mission is to manage our clients’ technology and mitigate their cyber risks, so that they don’t have to.

The Technical Project Manager, UCaaS owns the delivery of Harbor IT's unified communications and voice implementations from executed agreement through client handoff to support. This is a senior, client-facing role inside the UCaaS onboarding team. The person in this seat runs the full project lifecycle for cloud voice, contact center, and carrier migration work: kickoff and initiation, discovery and data collection, project planning, cutover execution, monitoring, training, and closeout. Unlike a general infrastructure PM, this role carries a real technical component. The Technical Project Manager must understand dial plans, number porting, call flow and routing design, session border controllers, network readiness and QoS, E911 compliance, and the dependencies between the voice platform and the underlying LAN, WAN, and firewall. They translate that technical detail into plans, risk registers, and change orders a client executive can act on. They direct project engineers, field technicians, trainers, carriers, and subcontractors without direct reporting authority. While the UCaaS practice is the primary focus, this role will also require exposure to or management of IT, data network, and/or cybersecurity projects as the delivery pipeline requires. Ultimately this person is accountable for the success or failure of assigned projects, for on-time and on-budget delivery, and for client satisfaction at handoff.

Key Responsibilities

Own UCaaS, cloud voice, contact center, and carrier migration projects end to end, from executed agreement through closeout and transition to the Support Center.
Serve as the client's primary point of contact across all project phases: kickoff and initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, and closeout.
Build and maintain project plans that identify scope, resources, tasks, dependencies, milestones, and timelines, and hold the plan current as conditions change.
Lead technical discovery and data collection for voice cutovers, including dial plan design, number inventory and porting, call flow and routing requirements, user and device provisioning, E911 and regulatory compliance, and network readiness assessment covering QoS, bandwidth, PoE, and firewall/SBC configuration.
Coordinate carrier and vendor activity including LOA submission, port scheduling, circuit delivery, and escalation, and hold carriers accountable to committed dates.
Plan and run cutover events including cutover runbooks, rollback criteria, after-hours execution windows, day-one support coverage, and post-cutover stabilization.
Document, quantify, and communicate project risk. Mitigate where possible or proceed under documented and accepted risk with client sign-off.
Schedule and direct project resources including project engineers, field technicians, trainers, associate PMs, carriers, and subcontractors, and delegate effectively without direct reporting authority.
Author and deliver project documentation including project plans, discovery questionnaires, cutover runbooks, training materials, change orders, as-built documentation, and signoff packages.
Manage project budget and margin, issue change orders for out-of-scope work, and prevent eroding project profitability from scope creep. .
Log hours and project detail in ConnectWise Manage accurately and on time, and keep client configuration records current in the customer database.
Escalate project and client issues to Client Success and Operations Management on a timely basis, and drive resolution rather than handing off the problem.
Support pre-sales when required by scoping project involvement, drafting statements of work, and budgeting project labor.
Contribute to the maturity of the project management practice through templates, methodology, scope-of-work improvements, and internal training on project workflow and internal process.
Maintain PMP or similar project management certification and current working knowledge of the UCaaS platforms Harbor IT delivers.

Qualifications & Skills

Demonstrated command of the full project management lifecycle including scope definition, planning, risk management, budget and change control, and formal closeout.
Hands-on working knowledge of UCaaS and cloud voice delivery: dial plan design, number porting and LNP, call routing and auto-attendant/IVR flow, SIP trunking, session border controllers, E911, and MACD processes.
Working knowledge of the network layer voice depends on, including QoS, VLAN segmentation, PoE, bandwidth planning, firewall and NAT traversal, and SD-WAN.
Proven ability to plan and execute cutover events with defined rollback criteria, including after-hours and weekend windows.
Excellent written and oral communication, including the ability to brief technologists, operations managers, and C-suite executives on the same project with the right level of detail for each.
Ability to hold carriers, vendors, and subcontractors accountable to committed dates and quality standards.
Comfort managing multiple concurrent projects across clients without dropping detail or missing commitments.
Proficiency with project management tooling such as Smartsheet, MS Project, and Microsoft Teams, and with PSA systems, ideally ConnectWise Manage.
Comfort operating in an EOS-managed, growth-stage MSP/MSSP environment with shared accountability across teams.

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in a technical or business discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
5 or more years managing technology implementation projects, with at least 3 years focused on voice, unified communications, or UCaaS delivery.
Direct delivery experience with one or more major UCaaS or cloud voice platforms, for example Intermedia Unite/Elevate, ZoomPhone, Cisco/Webex Calling, Microsoft Teams Phone, RingCentral, or 8x8.
Experience delivering projects in a managed services provider, VAR, telecom integrator, or carrier professional services environment.
PMP certification preferred. Platform and vendor certifications relevant to the UCaaS stack are a plus.
Experience with ConnectWise Manage PSA and preferred.

Work Environment

Reports to the Manager of UCaaS Onboarding within Harbor IT's professional services organization, operating under an EOS framework with shared accountability across delivery teams.
Hybrid role based out of the Framingham, MA headquarters with remote flexibility. Some local and regional client travel may be required (less than 10%).
Direct and frequent client exposure across mid-market and enterprise accounts. After-hours and occasional weekend work is required for cutover events and project deadlines.

Benefits

Competitive salary commensurate with experience
Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance.
401(k) retirement plan with company match
Unlimited PTO and standard holidays
Professional development opportunities

The Pay Range For This Role Is

80,000 - 95,000 USD per year (Harbor Networks)

● Plans and manages project activities for a variety of diverse and complex projects utilizing project management principles, methodologies, tools and techniques.

● Certificate in one of the main project management methodologies is an asset (e.g. PMI Certificate, PMP, Prince 2, CSM).
● Advanced hands-on knowledge and understanding of project management principles, methodologies, tools and techniques.
● Ability to think conceptually and analytically, conduct effective, thorough reviews of customer project requirements and deliverables, and manage projects and team resources of considerable size and complexity through to successful completion.
● Strong analytical, problem solving, organizational and time management skills.
● Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing with customers, business and technical teams and other co-workers; and adapt easily to changing priorities and business needs.

jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

We believe water is more than a resource, it's a shared responsibility. As part of our Water Business Group, you’ll help shape how communities manage water for generations to come. From delivering safe drinking water and treating wastewater responsibly to developing sustainable water supplies and protecting lives and property through flood control, your work will directly support public health, environmental sustainability, and infrastructure resilience. We bring together experts across disciplines to solve complex challenges with bold thinking and technical excellence. Whether you're modernizing aging systems or pioneering innovative approaches, your contributions will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. This isn’t just a job, it's a chance to lead change, drive progress, and leave a lasting legacy.

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

HDR is looking for an experienced practitioner in fisheries engineering, restoration, and ecohydraulics to be a part of our thriving team in the Pacific Northwest practice area. This is an opportunity to join an established, highly successful team already solving the most challenging fisheries related engineering work throughout the West Coast. The candidate will be responsible for providing technical expertise at the project level and assisting with growing HDRs fisheries program through development of client relationships and identification of opportunities for expansion of HDR s suite of environmental and water resource related services. Responsibilities will include technical work, mentoring, team building, project management, business development, and client management. The candidate will also be responsible for establishing technical and project management strategies that emphasize quality, staff development, client satisfaction, and financial responsibility utilizing HDRs technology, standards, and project delivery practices. The primary duties of this position include planning, directing, and monitoring all aspects of large multi-discipline projects or medium sized projects with high degree of technical complexity. The candidate will be involved with the production and coordination of several projects concurrently. This position offers additional opportunities for travel and working within other regions of practice across the United States and Canada.

In the role of Senior Project Manager - Fisheries
, we'll count on you to:

Direct and coordinate work of single or multidiscipline teams throughout the project's lifecycle (from development & initiation to close-out)
Responsible for all aspects of large multidiscipline projects or medium-sized projects with high degree of technical complexity, involving a large project staff
Produce and coordinate several projects concurrently
Establish and maintain client relations, and be involved with marketing, contractual, design and production meetings
Conduct work sessions for deliverable development in conjunction with other staff and stakeholders
Coordinate staffing and workload through entire project life cycle, and ensure completion of deliverables on schedule
Track financial aspects of projects, and coordinate and adjust work effort with team to ensure that work is completed within parameters of agreed-to budget and schedule
Work with the Accounting, Operational and Business leadership for periodic project reviews
Implement QA/QC procedures
Supervise large project staffs and act as mentor for less-experienced Project Managers
Perform other duties as needed

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing projects and tasks.
Experience performing planning, design development, contract documentation, preparation of plans and specifications construction engineering oversight on a wide variety of water resource projects.
Experience leading, directing, and mentoring technical staff. Experience interfacing with a broad range of science and engineering disciplines.
Experience conducting or managing 1D/2D/3D hydraulic modeling to support planning and design of a wide range of projects including stream rehabilitation and restoration, fish passage, fish behavior, screened surface water intakes, complex culverts and bridges, and floodplain management (planning and design).
Experience leading and participating in the preparation of technical and non-technical reports and presentations including visualization of data.
Experience with business development activities including client relations, marketing pursuits, and project proposals

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering
10 years related experience
A minimum 5 years project management experience
Requires professional engineering license recognized by the licensing board for the location of the position offered. Example: Professional Engineer (PE or P.Eng) license.
MS Office and MS Project experience (Access experience would be plus)
Demonstrated leadership, business development and strategic planning skills
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee ownership, employee health, performance, and success, which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time away, parental leave, paid holidays, a retirement savings plan with employer match, employee referral bonus and tuition reimbursement. jobs.description:
事業概要

すべての経済活動のデジタル化を目指す株式会社LayerXは、Ai Workforce事業部において、「AIを業務に溶け込ませる」をコンセプトとした生成AIプラットフォーム「Ai Workforce」を開発・提供しています。
Ai Workforce事業部は2023年に発足した新規事業チームであり、幅広い業界のエンタープライズ企業パートナーとの取り組みを積み重ねてきました。大規模言語モデル（LLM）などのAIの技術は飛躍的に発展していますが、それ単体では本格的な業務で使うことが難しく、そのギャップを埋めるUX (AI-UX) を実現することを目指しています。
実証実験（PoC）ではなく、プロダクトとして既に続々とお客様にご導入いただいており、AIのポテンシャルを活かす更なるプロダクトの進化や、市場の拡大に取り組んでいます。

募集背景

Ai Workforce事業部では、日本を代表する大手企業を対象に、生成AIプラットフォーム「Ai Workforce」を開発・提供しています。
デプロイメントストラテジストは、エンジニアと協同してプロジェクトをリードし、プラットフォームが提供する「ナレッジ」「スキル」「ツール」「UI」という4種類のコンポーネントを自在に組み合わせ、顧客・業界単位で最適なAIエージェントを創り上げることをミッションとしています。
金融業界は、「膨大な非構造データ」と「厳密なルール」に基づく情報産業であり、膨大な書類の確認・審査等の人間がテキストを読んで判断・作成する業務が多く、LLM導入により劇的なコスト削減や収益向上が見込める領域です。
金融機関は「産業の血液」とも言われます。金融という心臓部をLLMにより強化することで、日本産業全体を力強く駆動します。

業務内容

プロジェクトマネジメント: 顧客の業務プロセスやAI活用方針を深く分析し、AIエージェント構築のプロジェクト設計を行います。
AIエージェント設計: エンジニア（Forward Deployed Engineer）とペアを組み、Ai Workforceの4つのコンポーネント（ナレッジ、スキル、ツール、UI）を組み合わせ、顧客・業界単位で最適化されたAIエージェントを設計・構築します。
プロダクトマネジメント: 上記4つのコンポーネント自体の機能追加やバージョンアップに関するプロダクトマネジメントを担当します。
新規ソリューションの立ち上げ: 個々の案件で得られた知見を体系化し、業界・職務単位で汎用的な「ソリューション」として企画・開発します。

ポジションの魅力

コンサルタントとしての強みを土台に、自分自身の手で事業やプロダクトを作る経験やキャリアを構築できます。
エンジニア（Forward Deployed Engineer）と密接に協働し、AIの先端技術が大企業や社会に実装していく過程に深く関与できます。
国内有数の金融機関が競争優位性を構築する過程を自ら企画・実装し、変革の姿を目の当たりにすることができます。

必要な条件/経験

コンサルティングファームまたはそれに類する企業での勤務経験（3年以上）
エンジニアを巻き込み、大企業のプロジェクトマネジメントを行った経験
金融機関向けの提案・デリバリー経験

AIやデータサイエンスのプロジェクト経験
戦略コンサルタントとしての経験
日本語にてコミュニケーションが可能なこと / Native level－like fluency in Japanese

望ましい経験/スキル

プロダクトの企画やデザインに携わった経験（ユーザー視点で必要な機能・体験を考え、開発ロードマップに反映させたこと）
マネージャー以上の職位の経験
営業活動の経験

こんな方と働きたい

行動指針「徳 , Trustful Team , Bet AI , Fact Base ,Be Animal」に共感する方

As a Project Delivery PROJECT - Security Engineer II on the project, you will:

Technology Risk Research: Conduct targeted research on materiel, hardware components, and software utilized in Army systems. Evaluate the overarching risk to critical technologies.
Vulnerability & Threat Analysis: Identify specific vulnerabilities within proposed technologies. Analyze adversarial attack vectors and assess how foreign threats target DoD systems.
BOM Analysis: Deconstruct and analyze Bills of Materials (BOMs) for complex systems. Identify risky, compromised, or counterfeit components within the technical supply chain.
Systems Contextualization: Apply a deep understanding of Army weapons platforms and tactical systems. Translate abstract technical vulnerabilities into concrete operational risks.

The Team

Deloitte's Government & Public Services (GPS) practice - our people, ideas, technology and outcomes - is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.

Our Cyber Defense & Resilience offering assists clients in defending against advanced threats by transforming security operations, monitoring technology, data analytics, and threat intelligence. Helps manage and protect dynamic attack surfaces and provides rapid crisis and cyber incident response, ensuring clients can be ready for, respond to, and recover from business disruptions.

The Project Delivery Talent Model is designed for professionals with specialized skills that align to a current client need. In classified intelligence analysis, DoD or IC cyber threat research, or technical/cyber analysis in a classified environment.

Tradecraft: Proven ability to apply Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) and All-Source methodologies to technical problem sets. Experience with Technical Intelligence or classified Cyber Threat Intelligence is highly desired.

jobs.title: Corporate Security Analyst
jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

We're looking for a Corporate Security Analyst to join our rapidly growing CorpSec team. This role is for someone who is passionate about corporate security and building on existing frameworks, and is available to candidates local to one of our hubs (Burnaby, Calgary, or Toronto). You will be expected to be in-office a minimum of twice per week.

CorpSec is transitioning and growing at Clio into a focused, mission-driven function with security systems and practices already in place. Your team works closely with IT Systems, Application Security, People, Compliance, and IT Services to ensure appropriate security coverage in detection, response, and establishing non-adversarial techniques.

The Corporate Security Analyst will be responsible for adopting and unifying systems, communication, and oversight across IT Systems, Application Security, and Compliance. You will build upon existing trust, define a unified approach, and formalize the program in accordance with compliance requirements. You will build upon existing trust, work with a unified approach, and support the program in accordance with compliance requirements.

What you’ll do:

This role acts as an operator of Clio's corporate security toolset, owning the endpoint tools, investigative processes, and organizational culture required to protect Clio from internal and external threats - both accidental and intentional. You own the day-to-day execution: monitoring alerts, triaging DLP events, running investigations, and keeping the systems that protect Clio running reliably. You don't need to have all the answers - but you need to determine what you don't know, ask the right questions, and close the loop on everything you own.

Build & Run: Monitor and triage DLP alerts to surface real signals from noise and operate EDR day-to-day by reviewing detections and executing response procedures. You’re naturally curious about how the tools you operate actually work, not just how to use them.
Drive Education: Run phishing simulation campaigns end-to-end - from scheduling to employee education loops - while ensuring that no one is left guessing by communicating clearly when something breaks.
Incident Response: Handle L1/L2 security incidents (phishing, device compromise, data loss) by triaging and containing threats. You take pride in ensuring that alerts don’t age in your queue.
Optimize Systems: Maintain runbooks and support compliance evidence collection (SOC 2, ISO 27001). You adapt when priorities shift and don't need perfect information to make progress.
Technical Growth: Develop scripts to drive auto-remediation and tune security tooling for AI detection to address unauthorized data moves.
Collaborate: Engage with a security culture that solicits feedback and drives visibility across Clio’s security stack (Okta, 1Password, Google Workspace, MDM).

What you bring:

2-4 years of hands-on experience in a security operations, IT security, or endpoint support role.
Tool Proficiency: Hands-on experience with EDR, DLP, Phishing, SSO Platforms, or Google Workspace security controls.
Analytical Mindset: A healthy curiosity to look for the "why" and fix the problem rather than the symptom.
Communication: Clear, evidence-first written communication. You document what you did, what you found, and what you decided.
Judgment: You know when to figure something out independently and when to ask for help.
Demonstrate a keen interest in improving your craft by using AI

Bonus if you have:

Hands-on familiarity with MDM or SIEM in a security incident context.
Experience supporting SOC 2 or ISO 27001 evidence collection.
Exposure to scripting (Python, Bash) for automating investigation or remediation tasks.
Relevant certifications: CISSP, CompTIA Security+, CySA+, or equivalent.

This is a new role.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin, London, New York City and Sydney) to be in office min. twice per week.
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
$2000 annual counseling benefit
RRSP matching and RESP contribution
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

The expected salary range for this role is $119,000 to $161,000 CAD. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Vulnerability & Threat Analysis: Identify specific vulnerabilities within proposed technologies. Analyze adversarial attack vectors and assess how foreign threats target DoD systems.

Systems Contextualization: Apply a deep understanding of Army weapons platforms and tactical systems. Translate abstract technical vulnerabilities into concrete operational risks.

The Team

Deloitte's Government & Public Services (GPS) practice - our people, ideas, technology and outcomes - is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.

Our Cyber Defense & Resilience offering assists clients in defending against advanced threats by transforming security operations, monitoring technology, data analytics, and threat intelligence. In classified intelligence analysis, DoD or IC cyber threat research, or technical/cyber analysis in a classified environment.

jobs.description:
About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Information security is an integral part of Visa's corporate culture. It is essential to maintain our position as an industry leader in electronic payments, which is why Visa has made it a priority to create top-tier security operations and incident response teams to defend the company against evolving cyber threats. If you would like to join a company where security is truly valued, where you can work with like-minded peers who are passionate about the art & science of cyber defense, and where you can use state of the art tools for maximum impact, then we have a home for you.

The successful candidate will work with a team of incident responders at one of Visa's Cyber Fusion Centers. The team is part of a larger organization located across multiple geographical sites that are responsible for the comprehensive cyber defense of Visa and its subsidiaries.

Essential Functions

Manage and address cybersecurity incidents through all stages, including identification, containment, and eradication.
Perform deep-dive analysis on systems, accounts, and networks to identify the root cause and impact of incidents.
Act as an engagement point for broader technology teams, including Cyber Defense and Engineering.
Perform proactive threat hunting to identify and mitigate potential threats before they can cause harm.
Develop and refine detection rules to improve the identification and response to security incidents.
Provide detailed reports and documentation of incidents and response actions.
Conduct quality control of the work performed by analysts to ensure accuracy and thoroughness.
Mentor and train junior analysts in advanced incident response techniques, tactics, and procedures.
Develop and maintain incident response playbooks and runbooks to ensure standardized and efficient response processes.
Contribute to identifying process improvement opportunities to enhance security incident response processes.
Implement process automation to streamline incident response workflows and improve efficiency.
Support and manage cybersecurity projects to enhance overall security posture.

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

5+ years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or at least 2 years of work experience with an Advanced degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or 0 years of work experience with a PhD, OR 8+ years of relevant work experience.

Preferred Qualifications

6 or more years of work experience with a bachelor’s degree or 4 or more years of relevant experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or up to 3 years of relevant experience with a PhD.
Proven subject matter expertise in relevant areas, such as incident response, threat hunting, malware analysis, web application security or security engineering.
3+ years of Security Operations Center (SOC) work experience with a bachelor’s degree.

Experience working in an enterprise-level incident response team or security operations center.

Direct experience in handling cyber security incidents and associated incident response tools.
Strong working knowledge of common security tools such as SIEM, AV, WAF, IDS, Netflow, Packet Analyzer and Endpoint Detection & Response tools.

Excellent understanding of DDoS techniques and mitigation mechanisms.
Display great problem-solving skills, with tenacity and resilience to resolve issues.
Excellent communication and presentation skills with proven skill in presenting analytical data effectively to varied audiences.
Strong interpersonal and leadership skills to influence and build credibility as a peer.
Strong understanding of cloud technologies and related security best practices.

jobs.description:
Offensive Security Analyst (Structured / Non-Exploit) — AI Training

About The Role

What if your deep understanding of how attackers think could directly shape how AI reasons about cybersecurity threats? We're looking for offensive security professionals to analyze real-world attack paths, adversary behavior, and defensive gaps — helping train and evaluate the next generation of AI systems.

This role is about structured adversarial reasoning, not exploit development. No CVEs, no shellcode — just sharp, methodical thinking about how threats move through real environments and where defenses break down.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role built for experienced security professionals who want meaningful, high-impact work on their own schedule.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Hourly Contract
Location: Remote
Commitment: 10–40 hours/week

What You'll Do

Analyze attack paths, kill chains, and adversary strategies across realistic, real-world system scenarios
Identify and classify weaknesses, misconfigurations, and defensive gaps that attackers would exploit
Review red-team-style scenarios and intrusion narratives for technical accuracy and depth
Generate, label, and validate adversarial reasoning data used to train and evaluate AI systems
Articulate complex attack chains, business impact, and risk tradeoffs in clear, structured language

You understand how real attacks unfold in production environments — not just in theory

Detail-oriented and methodical — you spot what others miss
Comfortable working independently and asynchronously without close supervision

Familiarity with frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK, Cyber Kill Chain, or STRIDE
Experience writing threat models, purple team reports, or adversary simulation documentation
Background in cloud security, Active Directory attacks, or network intrusion scenarios
Prior exposure to AI tools, data labeling, or security research writing

Why Join Us

Work directly on frontier AI systems alongside leading research labs
Fully remote and flexible — work when and where it suits you
Freelance autonomy with the structure of meaningful, task-based work
Apply your offensive security expertise to a domain where it creates lasting, large-scale impact
Potential for ongoing work and contract extension as new projects launch

jobs.title: Corporate Security Analyst
jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

We're looking for a Corporate Security Analyst to join our rapidly growing CorpSec team. This role is for someone who is passionate about corporate security and building on existing frameworks, and is available to candidates local to one of our hubs (Burnaby, Calgary, or Toronto). You will be expected to be in-office a minimum of twice per week.

CorpSec is transitioning and growing at Clio into a focused, mission-driven function with security systems and practices already in place. Your team works closely with IT Systems, Application Security, People, Compliance, and IT Services to ensure appropriate security coverage in detection, response, and establishing non-adversarial techniques.

The Corporate Security Analyst will be responsible for adopting and unifying systems, communication, and oversight across IT Systems, Application Security, and Compliance. You will build upon existing trust, define a unified approach, and formalize the program in accordance with compliance requirements. You will build upon existing trust, work with a unified approach, and support the program in accordance with compliance requirements.

What you’ll do:

This role acts as an operator of Clio's corporate security toolset, owning the endpoint tools, investigative processes, and organizational culture required to protect Clio from internal and external threats - both accidental and intentional. You own the day-to-day execution: monitoring alerts, triaging DLP events, running investigations, and keeping the systems that protect Clio running reliably. You don't need to have all the answers - but you need to determine what you don't know, ask the right questions, and close the loop on everything you own.

Build & Run: Monitor and triage DLP alerts to surface real signals from noise and operate EDR day-to-day by reviewing detections and executing response procedures. You’re naturally curious about how the tools you operate actually work, not just how to use them.
Drive Education: Run phishing simulation campaigns end-to-end - from scheduling to employee education loops - while ensuring that no one is left guessing by communicating clearly when something breaks.
Incident Response: Handle L1/L2 security incidents (phishing, device compromise, data loss) by triaging and containing threats. You take pride in ensuring that alerts don’t age in your queue.
Optimize Systems: Maintain runbooks and support compliance evidence collection (SOC 2, ISO 27001). You adapt when priorities shift and don't need perfect information to make progress.
Technical Growth: Develop scripts to drive auto-remediation and tune security tooling for AI detection to address unauthorized data moves.
Collaborate: Engage with a security culture that solicits feedback and drives visibility across Clio’s security stack (Okta, 1Password, Google Workspace, MDM).

What you bring:

2-4 years of hands-on experience in a security operations, IT security, or endpoint support role.
Tool Proficiency: Hands-on experience with EDR, DLP, Phishing, SSO Platforms, or Google Workspace security controls.
Analytical Mindset: A healthy curiosity to look for the "why" and fix the problem rather than the symptom.
Communication: Clear, evidence-first written communication. You document what you did, what you found, and what you decided.
Judgment: You know when to figure something out independently and when to ask for help.
Demonstrate a keen interest in improving your craft by using AI

Bonus if you have:

Hands-on familiarity with MDM or SIEM in a security incident context.
Experience supporting SOC 2 or ISO 27001 evidence collection.
Exposure to scripting (Python, Bash) for automating investigation or remediation tasks.
Relevant certifications: CISSP, CompTIA Security+, CySA+, or equivalent.

This is a new role.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin, London, New York City and Sydney) to be in office min. twice per week.
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
$2000 annual counseling benefit
RRSP matching and RESP contribution
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

The expected salary range for this role is $119,000 to $161,000 CAD. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Clio provides accessibility accommodations during the recruitment process. Should you require any accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Learn more about our culture at clio.com/careers

We're a Human and High Performing AI company, meaning we use artificial intelligence to improve all of our operations. In recruitment, AI helps us streamline the process for greater efficiency. However, we've built our systems to ensure that a human always reviews AI-generated output, and we never make automated hiring decisions.

We only communicate with candidates through official @clio.com email addresses.

jobs.title: Compliance Program Manager
jobs.description:
Job Title:
Compliance Program Manager

Company:
AISIN World Corp. of America

Department:
General Administration, Legal Affairs Department

Location:
Northville, MI

Position Summary

AISIN World Corp. of America ("AWA"), a global Tier-1 automotive supplier, is seeking a Compliance Program Manager to join our Legal Affairs Department.

This position brings the compliance program to the people who do the work. You will build and deliver compliance training, roll out new policies across more than 30 companies in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and promote the program so more than 15,000 team members understand the standards, why they matter, and how to raise a concern.

The successful candidate brings at least five years of compliance experience and communicates equally effectively on the plant floor and in the executive suite. You are organized, you follow through, and you can analyze program data and explain what it means.

A law degree is not required, though an attorney would be well suited to this role. Our attorneys handle legal advice, legal risk, the compliance hotline, and investigations. Your focus is to build the program, operate it, and establish it across our plants and offices.

The position requires approximately 25% travel to our sites in the United States, Mexico, and Canada. We welcome candidates who want to grow into a global compliance leadership role.

Position Responsibilities

The Compliance Program Manager is expected to perform the following three core functions that the company has determined are essential to this position:

Compliance Program Ownership and Network Leadership

Run the day-to-day operation of the North American compliance program. It covers more than 30 companies in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The program and all materials are delivered in English, Spanish, and Japanese.
Be the main contact for compliance program questions from our companies and from Japan headquarters. Send legal questions to Legal Affairs.
Lead the network of Compliance Officers and Compliance Managers at each company. They do not report to you. You lead them through trust, clear standards, and follow-up.
Deliver standard training to every Compliance Officer and Compliance Manager. Cover their duties, including Code of Conduct work, policy rollout, training delivery, and when to escalate. Teach in person and online, track 100% completion, and maintain the records.
Visit plants and offices to see how the program is working. Meet with local leaders and team members, and share your observations with Legal Affairs.
Work with the Japan headquarters compliance team. This includes weekly calls on the status of compliance activities and promoting compliance materials.
Some calls may be late at night or early in the morning.

Report program status and results to the General Counsel, Senior Counsel, senior management, and Japan headquarters management. Reporting is ongoing and driven by need, not only on a fixed schedule.
Write the annual compliance program report and recommend the program priorities for the next fiscal year.

Training, Communication, and Culture

Manage the Code of Conduct program. This includes annual training, new hire onboarding, and updates. Legal Affairs reviews and approves all content before release.
Plan, schedule, and deliver annual training on compliance topics, policies, and procedures across the company:
Code of Conduct
Antitrust
Anti-corruption and bribery
Other compliance topics identified for the year
Executive, management, and Compliance Officer training

Plan and track training across all locations and employee groups, and drive completion to the annual target.
Build compliance campaigns and materials that work for a plant floor audience. This includes posters, short messages, and site events.
Have all materials translated into Spanish and Japanese. Check the translations before they go out.
Speak to senior leaders, HR groups, company compliance meetings, and Japan headquarters as the region's expert on the compliance program.
Run the annual compliance survey from start to finish. Study the results and present what you found and what to do about it to Legal Affairs and senior management.

Policy Rollout and Program Support

Maintain the regional compliance policy library.
Work with each company to put the regional policies in place and track them through to completion.
Roll out approved policies and procedures across the company. Legal Affairs writes the policies. You take them to the organizations and ensure adoption.
Prepare the proposal for senior management approval.
Explain the change across a large network of companies.
Build and deliver training for office and plant employees.

Own the compliance program records for the region. This includes training completion, policy sign-offs, and site visit records. Keep the data accurate and audit-ready.
Support compliance technology projects, including self-service and AI tools. Verify content accuracy before release, and monitor tool usage.
Manage compliance program vendors, including training platforms and translation providers. Watch service levels, scheduling, invoices, and performance.
Help Legal Affairs manage outside law firms on compliance matters. This includes scheduling, collecting documents, tracking status, and tracking budget. Legal Affairs hires and directs outside counsel.

Perform other duties and tasks assigned. This job description is not intended to be a complete list of all responsibilities, and duties may change as business needs require.

Required Skills And Abilities

Essential Skills and Experience:

ABILITY TO PROJECT-MANAGE LARGE-SCALE COMPLIANCE ROLLOUTS AND PROJECTS REQUIRED
No less than 5 years of proven experience in compliance or ethics.
No less than 5 years of proven experience promoting, rolling out, and building support for a company compliance program.
Must be a dynamic speaker and presenter; a people person. You will present to large groups regularly.
Proven ability to lead and get results from people who do not report to you.
Experience building training and teaching live to large, mixed groups, including hourly plant employees.
Ability to pull, study, and explain program data, such as training completion rates and survey results.
Skilled in PowerPoint and able to present ideas clearly.
Strong communication skills in speaking, writing, and presenting. Effective with senior executives and with plant floor employees.
Able to work on your own and take initiative.
Strong organization and time management skills, with close attention to detail.
Proven ability to drive open items to completion across many sites and time zones.

Beneficial Skills And Experience

Experience promoting compliance activities to a plant workforce.
Experience training and teaching a workforce about compliance.
Experience promoting compliance materials in more than one language, including checking translation quality.
Working knowledge of Spanish or Japanese.
Experience at a Japanese-parented company or another company with a foreign headquarters.
Experience running a learning management system or other compliance records system.
Experience with compliance technology, including self-service or AI tools.
Experience visiting or auditing manufacturing sites.

Education/Training/Certifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.
Certified Compliance and Ethics Professional (CCEP or CCEP-I) preferred. If you are not certified, you must earn it within 12 months of hire. The company will pay for study materials and the exam.
A law degree is not required, but it is a plus.

jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a GRC - Security Analyst based in India.

This role supports the organization’s cybersecurity governance, risk, and compliance program, helping identify and manage security risks across technology, vendors, and business processes. You will contribute to the development and maintenance of security policies, controls, and governance practices while supporting audits and compliance assessments. The position provides broad exposure to frameworks such as SOC 2, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS, depending on business requirements. You will collaborate closely with Information Security, IT, Legal, Privacy, Internal Audit, and business stakeholders to translate security issues into actionable business risks. The role also involves third-party risk management, evidence collection, remediation tracking, and security reporting. This is an opportunity for a detail-oriented cybersecurity professional to strengthen security maturity while continuously improving GRC processes and automation.

Accountabilities

Perform cybersecurity and technology risk assessments across systems, applications, vendors, and business processes, documenting risks and evaluating their potential business impact.
Maintain information security policies, standards, procedures, control frameworks, risk registers, and governance documentation.
Support compliance activities aligned with frameworks and regulations such as SOC 2, HIPAA, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and other applicable requirements.
Assist with internal and external audits, regulatory examinations, security assessments, and customer compliance reviews by gathering, validating, and maintaining control evidence.
Track audit findings, security risks, control deficiencies, exceptions, and remediation plans through resolution, working with control owners to assess effectiveness and implement improvements.
Conduct third-party and vendor security assessments, including reviewing security questionnaires, certifications, audit reports, and supporting documentation.
Support security awareness, policy acknowledgment, risk acceptance, and security exception processes while responding to customer and partner due diligence requests.
Monitor changes in regulatory requirements, security standards, and cybersecurity practices and help translate relevant developments into governance improvements.
Develop GRC metrics, dashboards, reports, and management documentation to communicate security and compliance status effectively.
Partner with technical security teams to translate vulnerabilities and technical security issues into clear business risks and identify opportunities to automate and improve GRC processes.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Information Systems, Risk Management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
3+ years of experience in cybersecurity, governance, risk management, compliance, IT audit, or a related discipline.
Relevant certification such as Security+, CISA, CRISC, or CGRC is preferred.
Working knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks and standards such as HITRUST, SOC 2, PCI DSS, or comparable frameworks.
Experience performing security risk assessments and evaluating the effectiveness of security controls.
Familiarity with regulatory and compliance requirements relevant to technology-driven organizations.
Some experience or exposure to incident response, with a strong interest in cybersecurity and a willingness to continuously learn.
Strong analytical, organizational, planning, documentation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple assessments, findings, and deadlines.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain security, compliance, and risk concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Strong attention to detail, ability to meet deadlines, and proficiency with Microsoft Office or comparable productivity and reporting tools.
Curiosity about emerging technology and cybersecurity trends, with the ability to identify practical opportunities for improving security and IT infrastructure.

Benefits

Fully remote work arrangement in India.
Full-time opportunity within an Information Technology and cybersecurity environment.
Exposure to enterprise-wide cybersecurity governance, risk, compliance, and audit activities.
Hands-on experience with recognized security frameworks including SOC 2, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS.
Opportunity to work cross-functionally with Information Security, IT, Legal, Privacy, Internal Audit, and business teams.
Broad experience in third-party risk management, security assessments, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance.
Opportunity to contribute to GRC automation, process improvement, reporting, and security maturity initiatives.

jobs.description:
Introduction

When you join the Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS), you join a team of more than 5,000 employees across the state dedicated to positively changing the lives of more than 1 million Marylanders each year. We do this by providing economic support, preventive services, and caring for children and adults.

We aim to deliver services so that we more quickly meet the needs of the people we serve. At DHS, we grapple with hard questions to find new ways to foster a culture of bold innovation. We do this to ensure that in Maryland, we leave no one behind.

This is a Management Service position that serves at the pleasure of the Appointing Authority.

GRADE

20

LOCATION OF POSITION

Maryland Department of Human Services

Division of Administrative Operations

S. Charles St.

Baltimore, MD 21201

Main Purpose of Job

The Deputy Director of the Office of Emergency Operations directs and coordinates the Department's emergency preparation, response and recovery operations statewide as mandated by the State Emergency Operations Plan (SEOP), both during steady-state and emergency operations. The position establishes statewide emergency operations plans and policies and oversees the implementation of such plans and policies at DHS Central and at the LDSSs as required by local plans and directives. This position manages 9 staff positions permanently assigned to the Office of Emergency Operations, and supervises additional staff assigned to emergency operations during an emergency event.

POSITION DUTIES

Develop, implement and administrate the federal, state and local emergency response plans and systems for DHS's Central office and the 24 local Departments of Social Services.
Coordinate, review, and update the mandated Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) for DHS and the local departments to ensure the readiness of all relocation and command center sites, communication devices, and support equipment as certified by the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM).
Develop hazard plans, conduct risk and vulnerability assessments, and coordinate training and preparedness initiatives to mitigate potential emergencies.
Direct and manage the implementation of the State Administrative Plan (SAP) for Individual Assistance (IA) in coordination with the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDE.M) and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).
Communicate with all levels of management concerning the preparations and response to emergency situations.
Communicate and coordinate with facility managers and contractors to ensure back-up power capacity and costs associated with back-up power provisions for communication and operation of State shelters during an emergency incident.
Coordinate and/or attend meetings, briefings, conferences, and seminars sponsored by federal, State, and local emergency management agencies as well as partner organizations and outside experts in the field.
Train the emergency operations coordinators throughout the department.
Facilitate meetings of federal, State and local emergency management agencies and other partner agencies, e.g. American Red Cross, for the purpose of ensuring the availability of resources for mass care, sheltering, and emergency assistance for the citizens and visitors of Maryland as a result of a natural or man-made disaster.
Manage State Shelter Containers (FEMA Shelter Containers were transferred from MDEM to DHS).
Oversee the maintenance of State shelter information database. The database is to be reviewed and updated annually.
Conduct annual updates of the local shelter supplies, etc., working in conjunction with the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the local school superintendents.
Conduct annual State shelter site visits to ensure the continued viability of the facility to be utilized as a state shelter site during or after a natural or man-made disaster.

Minimum Qualifications

Education:
A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.

Description

The Carrier Services team is seeking a Supply Strategy Analyst to support data-driven decision-making for Amazon's Canada middle mile transportation network. This role will pull and analyze supply program data, support load distribution reporting across dedicated 3P carrier programs and Amazon's RLB/RFA auction and Day Rate supply types, and prepare analysis that helps the team balance cost efficiency with network capacity. The ideal candidate is comfortable working with large datasets, proficient in SQL and Excel, and able to turn data into clear, accurate reports and summaries.

Key job responsibilities

Pull and consolidate supply program data across Day Rate, Relay Freight Auction, and Relay Load Board supply types to support weekly, quarterly, and annual planning cycles
Prepare and maintain Weekly Business Review (WBR) reporting and the Canada Supply Flash, including variance summaries and trend analysis
Support documentation and standardization of Canada supply planning processes, including Plan of Record (POR) tracking and HVE planning cycles — demand signal inputs and supply mix rightsizing.
Track weekly volume forecasts by monitoring accuracy against actuals and flagging variances to the planning team
Gather and compile MM linehaul demand and capacity inputs for the Canada Network Optimization run, coordinating data collection across Finance, CTS, and Supply Planning teams
Support documentation and standardization of Canada supply planning processes, including Plan of Record (POR) tracking
Identify and flag data integrity issues and coordinate with relevant teams to resolve them
Coordinate data collection from Finance, MMPO, CTS, and Supply Planning teams to meet planning deadlines
Respond to ad hoc data and reporting requests from team leads and stakeholders

About The Team

Amazon Transportation Services is focused on building reliable, cost-effective transportation capacity across our network. The Canada Supply Strategy team supports planning and optimization of middle mile carrier programs to ensure Amazon can move freight efficiently across Canada. This role plays a key part in keeping our reporting accurate and our planning inputs on time. Come join us and help power data-driven decisions in a fast-moving logistics environment.

High school or equivalent diploma
Knowledge of Excel at an intermediate level (e.g., pivot tables & charts, multiple criteria lookups, nested logical/IF formulas, data cleansing, array formulas, etc.)
Experience managing large data sets and utilizing to drive performance and process improvements

Preferred Qualifications

1+ years of program management, logistics, operations, supply chain, transportation, or equivalent experience
1+ years of management experience
Bachelor's degree
Experience with SQL

Experience analysing and interpreting complex datasets.
Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify risks, drive improvements and deliver outcomes.

Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
