new_jobs.title: Sr. Business Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Opentext - The Information Company

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.

AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.

At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.

YOUR IMPACT

OpenText is seeking a naturally curious and analytical professional to join the Cash Flow Planning & Analysis team in Richmond Hill. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, working with data, and uncovering insights that drive better business decisions. Whether your background is in finance, accounting, economics, engineering, computer science, or another quantitative discipline, success in this role comes from your ability to ask the right questions, connect the dots, and uncover answers that others might miss.

In this role, you'll work with large and complex datasets across multiple business systems to explain financial performance, improve forecasting accuracy, and identify opportunities to enhance business results. You'll investigate trends, determine root causes, challenge assumptions, and transform data into actionable insights that influence strategic decision-making. If you're energized by turning data into meaningful stories and enjoy making a measurable impact in a global organization, you'll thrive at OpenText.

What The Role Offers

An analytical thinker who enjoys breaking down complex problems and understanding how things work.
Ability to work quickly in a fast-paced environment, work comfortably with ambiguous requirements, and work with large data sets from multiple systems.
Self-starter who takes ownership, demonstrates initiative, and is motivated by continuous learning and improvement.
An effective communicator who can translate complex analysis into clear, actionable business insights.
Strong interest in technology, automation, AI tools, data analytics, process design, and innovation.
Data analysis and forecasting of receipts, disbursements, and other cash flow activity to identify trends, explain variances, and deliver meaningful business insights.
Support quarterly financial results by investigating outcomes, validating data, and providing analysis to Finance leadership.
Lead investigations into unexpected results, operational issues, and data anomalies, identifying root causes and recommending corrective actions.
Identify opportunities to improve reporting, analytics, processes, and data quality through automation, coding, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Contribute to special projects and strategic initiatives that require strong analytical thinking and sound business judgment.

What You Need To Succeed

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Finance, Accounting, Business, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
3+ years of experience in business analysis, financial analysis, data analysis, consulting, operations, corporate finance, accounting, or a related analytical discipline.
Proven ability to analyze complex datasets, identify patterns, investigate issues, and develop data-driven recommendations.
Hands-on experience with ERP systems and at least one data analytics, programming, or business intelligence technology such as Power BI, SQL, Python, Alteryx, Tableau, or Power Query is strongly preferred.
The successful candidate should be comfortable using technology to integrate data, automate recurring analysis, validate results, and improve forecasting and decision-making.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and operate effectively in an environment where problems are not always clearly defined.
Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to engage effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

ONE LAST THING

Join OpenText's Cash Flow Planning & Analysis team and play a key role in shaping business decisions through data-driven insights. This exciting opportunity is ideal for a naturally curious and analytical professional who enjoys solving complex problems, uncovering trends, and turning data into meaningful business recommendations. Working with large and diverse datasets, you'll help explain financial performance, improve forecasting accuracy, drive process improvements, and support strategic initiatives using analytics, automation, and innovative technologies. OpenText is looking for a proactive self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys continuous learning, and can translate complex analysis into actionable insights that create measurable impact across a global organization.

OpenText's commitment to diversity and inclusion surpasses legal requirements, evident in our Equal Employment Opportunity Statement of Policy which promotes a respectful and empowering environment for employees of all backgrounds, culture, national origin, race, color, gender, gender identification, sexual orientation, family status, age, veteran status, disability, religion, or other basis protected by applicable laws.

If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please contact us at hr@opentext.com. Our proactive approach fosters collaboration, innovation, and personal growth, enriching OpenText's vibrant workplace.

Compensation:
At OpenText, we offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package that supports your physical, emotional, and financial wellbeing. A summary of those benefits can be found on our Why Join Us page. As you move through the hiring process, we’re happy to provide more details about our compensation programs, including variable and commission compensation opportunities for eligible roles, vacation entitlement, and paid time off.

$x - $x; Depending on the candidate’s education, experience, skills, geographical location, and alignment with internal equity and external market, actual salary may vary and be higher or lower than the range posted.

new_jobs.title: IT Security Analyst I
new_jobs.description:
Description

The Information Technology department is hiring an IT Security Analyst I for the Security Operations team. You will be an important member of the team that helps manage IT security across the enterprise of 9,000+ employees. This position could be a good fit for you if you are looking to use your information security skills in a role that serves the community and offers opportunity for career growth.

As an IT Security Analyst I, you will be responsible for protecting Hennepin County’s information systems by monitoring, detecting, and responding to security incidents. As a member of our tierless Security Operations Center (SOC), you will follow the full cycle of security incidents. You will collaborate with other technical and business staff to identify and remediate risks while supporting an agile, innovative technology environment. Incumbents must continuously learn and adapt to an ever-changing risk landscape, stay current on changing security tools, tactics, techniques, and procedures. They must demonstrate a passion for the security area of information technology and be driven to protect Hennepin County.

Current Hennepin County employees who refer a candidate hired into an open competitive position may be eligible for a $500
referral bonus. For more information visit the employee referral program page.

Location and hours:

This position is remote. Remote workers may be required to come on-site 0 to 12 days a year for work meetings, trainings, or for any other reasons that their supervisor may deem necessary (may include additional days for onboarding and new employee training). Supervisors will provide as much advance notice as practicable. Work hours will be Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Based on business needs of this position, hires must live in or relocate to Minnesota. New Employee Orientation (NEO) for all new benefit-earning employees is in-person in downtown Minneapolis. Details about NEO will be provided upon hire.

About This Position Type

This is a full-time, benefit earning position.

This position is internally classified as an Information Technology (IT) Analyst Level I - Security Analyst in an Information Technology (IT) Analyst job class.

Click here to view the job classification specification.

In This Position, You Will

Serve as a member of the Information Security/Security Operations Team.
Serve in and support the Security Operations Center.
Analyze data from log correlation, threat intelligence, and SIEM tool(s) to identify, correlate, and mitigate risks to the Hennepin County cyber infrastructure.
Identify, investigate, and mitigate information security risks in coordination with other information security staff.
Participate in relevant information security projects.

Need to have:

One of the following:
Four years or more of experience in information technology.
Completion of approved IT Hennepin County internship and two years or more of IT experience .
Completion of five college/vocational technical technology courses and two years or more of IT experience .
Associate's/vocational/technical degree in computer science, management information systems (MIS), information technology or an approved information technology field related to the position and two years or more of IT experience.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, management information systems (MIS), information technology or an approved information technology field related to the position.

Nice to have:

Cybersecurity certificate (CompTIA Security+, CySA+, Network+, and/or other relevant certificates).
Experience:
Working in a local government organization.
Analyzing security events and responding to security incidents in a corporate environment.
Analyzing emails for potential cybersecurity threats.
Using Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools.
Working in cross-platform environments, networks, etc.

Ability to:
Analyze and resolve complex problems with computer operations or applications.
Work independently and in a team environment.
Learn and apply software and hardware troubleshooting techniques.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.

About the department:

Technology is the foundation of our work – and the work of every county employee. The Information Technology department is here to help our employees work smarter, faster and better. It is made up of 9 divisions: Business Solutions, Service Management Office, Architecture, Central Services Administration & Imaging Operations, Enterprise Development, IT Finance & Support Services, Operations, IT Strategic Alignment, and IT Security.

About Hennepin County

Hennepin is the largest county government organization in Minnesota. Our employees work every day to improve the health, safety and quality of life for our residents and communities. All of our jobs align with our mission to serve residents through transformative services that eliminate disparities, eliminate inequities, and create opportunity for all and our vision of a community where all people are healthy, all people are valued, and all people thrive.

Our employees receive a combination of competitive benefits and positive workplace culture. This includes meaningful work that impacts our community, competitive pay, work-life balance, a variety of benefits and opportunities to grow. Learn more at The Bridge (login as Guest).

Hennepin County envisions an organization where our commitment to diversity and the elimination of disparities is fundamental in providing excellent service to our community.

Your future. Made here.

All candidates for IT department positions must pass a fingerprint-based criminal background check prior to hire and maintain eligibility for Level 3 access to Criminal Justice Information (CJI), as required by the Minnesota BCA and FBI CJIS Security Policy. These roles may involve access to sensitive data and systems, and continued employment is contingent upon successful completion of CJIS training, adherence to security protocols, and periodic background rechecks.

new_jobs.title: Corporate Security Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

We're looking for a Corporate Security Analyst to join our rapidly growing CorpSec team. This role is for someone who is passionate about corporate security and building on existing frameworks, and is available to candidates local to one of our hubs (Burnaby, Calgary, or Toronto). You will be expected to be in-office a minimum of twice per week.

CorpSec is transitioning and growing at Clio into a focused, mission-driven function with security systems and practices already in place. Your team works closely with IT Systems, Application Security, People, Compliance, and IT Services to ensure appropriate security coverage in detection, response, and establishing non-adversarial techniques.

The Corporate Security Analyst will be responsible for adopting and unifying systems, communication, and oversight across IT Systems, Application Security, and Compliance. You will build upon existing trust, define a unified approach, and formalize the program in accordance with compliance requirements. You will build upon existing trust, work with a unified approach, and support the program in accordance with compliance requirements.

What you’ll do:

This role acts as an operator of Clio's corporate security toolset, owning the endpoint tools, investigative processes, and organizational culture required to protect Clio from internal and external threats - both accidental and intentional. You own the day-to-day execution: monitoring alerts, triaging DLP events, running investigations, and keeping the systems that protect Clio running reliably. You don't need to have all the answers - but you need to determine what you don't know, ask the right questions, and close the loop on everything you own.

Build & Run: Monitor and triage DLP alerts to surface real signals from noise and operate EDR day-to-day by reviewing detections and executing response procedures. You’re naturally curious about how the tools you operate actually work, not just how to use them.
Drive Education: Run phishing simulation campaigns end-to-end - from scheduling to employee education loops - while ensuring that no one is left guessing by communicating clearly when something breaks.
Incident Response: Handle L1/L2 security incidents (phishing, device compromise, data loss) by triaging and containing threats. You take pride in ensuring that alerts don’t age in your queue.
Optimize Systems: Maintain runbooks and support compliance evidence collection (SOC 2, ISO 27001). You adapt when priorities shift and don't need perfect information to make progress.
Technical Growth: Develop scripts to drive auto-remediation and tune security tooling for AI detection to address unauthorized data moves.
Collaborate: Engage with a security culture that solicits feedback and drives visibility across Clio’s security stack (Okta, 1Password, Google Workspace, MDM).

What you bring:

2-4 years of hands-on experience in a security operations, IT security, or endpoint support role.
Tool Proficiency: Hands-on experience with EDR, DLP, Phishing, SSO Platforms, or Google Workspace security controls.
Analytical Mindset: A healthy curiosity to look for the "why" and fix the problem rather than the symptom.
Communication: Clear, evidence-first written communication. You document what you did, what you found, and what you decided.
Judgment: You know when to figure something out independently and when to ask for help.
Demonstrate a keen interest in improving your craft by using AI

Bonus if you have:

Hands-on familiarity with MDM or SIEM in a security incident context.
Experience supporting SOC 2 or ISO 27001 evidence collection.
Exposure to scripting (Python, Bash) for automating investigation or remediation tasks.
Relevant certifications: CISSP, CompTIA Security+, CySA+, or equivalent.

This is a new role.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin, London, New York City and Sydney) to be in office min. twice per week.
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
$2000 annual counseling benefit
RRSP matching and RESP contribution
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

The expected salary range for this role is $119,000 to $161,000 CAD. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Clio provides accessibility accommodations during the recruitment process. Should you require any accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Learn more about our culture at clio.com/careers

However, we've built our systems to ensure that a human always reviews AI-generated output, and we never make automated hiring decisions.

Job Title:
Compliance Program Manager

Company:
AISIN World Corp. of America

Department:
General Administration, Legal Affairs Department

Location:
Northville, MI

Position Summary

AISIN World Corp. of America ("AWA"), a global Tier-1 automotive supplier, is seeking a Compliance Program Manager to join our Legal Affairs Department.

This position brings the compliance program to the people who do the work. You will build and deliver compliance training, roll out new policies across more than 30 companies in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and promote the program so more than 15,000 team members understand the standards, why they matter, and how to raise a concern.

The successful candidate brings at least five years of compliance experience and communicates equally effectively on the plant floor and in the executive suite. You are organized, you follow through, and you can analyze program data and explain what it means.

A law degree is not required, though an attorney would be well suited to this role. Our attorneys handle legal advice, legal risk, the compliance hotline, and investigations. Your focus is to build the program, operate it, and establish it across our plants and offices.

The position requires approximately 25% travel to our sites in the United States, Mexico, and Canada. We welcome candidates who want to grow into a global compliance leadership role.

Position Responsibilities

The Compliance Program Manager is expected to perform the following three core functions that the company has determined are essential to this position:

Compliance Program Ownership and Network Leadership

Run the day-to-day operation of the North American compliance program. It covers more than 30 companies in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The program and all materials are delivered in English, Spanish, and Japanese.
Be the main contact for compliance program questions from our companies and from Japan headquarters. Send legal questions to Legal Affairs.
Lead the network of Compliance Officers and Compliance Managers at each company. They do not report to you. You lead them through trust, clear standards, and follow-up.
Deliver standard training to every Compliance Officer and Compliance Manager. Cover their duties, including Code of Conduct work, policy rollout, training delivery, and when to escalate. Teach in person and online, track 100% completion, and maintain the records.
Visit plants and offices to see how the program is working. Meet with local leaders and team members, and share your observations with Legal Affairs.
Work with the Japan headquarters compliance team. This includes weekly calls on the status of compliance activities and promoting compliance materials.
Some calls may be late at night or early in the morning.

Report program status and results to the General Counsel, Senior Counsel, senior management, and Japan headquarters management. Reporting is ongoing and driven by need, not only on a fixed schedule.
Write the annual compliance program report and recommend the program priorities for the next fiscal year.

Training, Communication, and Culture

Plan, schedule, and deliver annual training on compliance topics, policies, and procedures across the company:
Code of Conduct
Antitrust

Executive, management, and Compliance Officer training

Plan and track training across all locations and employee groups, and drive completion to the annual target.
Build compliance campaigns and materials that work for a plant floor audience. This includes posters, short messages, and site events.
Have all materials translated into Spanish and Japanese. Check the translations before they go out.
Speak to senior leaders, HR groups, company compliance meetings, and Japan headquarters as the region's expert on the compliance program.
Run the annual compliance survey from start to finish. Study the results and present what you found and what to do about it to Legal Affairs and senior management.

Policy Rollout and Program Support

Maintain the regional compliance policy library.
Work with each company to put the regional policies in place and track them through to completion.
Roll out approved policies and procedures across the company. Legal Affairs writes the policies. You take them to the organizations and ensure adoption.
Prepare the proposal for senior management approval.

Build and deliver training for office and plant employees.

Support compliance technology projects, including self-service and AI tools. Verify content accuracy before release, and monitor tool usage.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a GRC - Security Analyst based in India.

This role supports the organization’s cybersecurity governance, risk, and compliance program, helping identify and manage security risks across technology, vendors, and business processes. You will contribute to the development and maintenance of security policies, controls, and governance practices while supporting audits and compliance assessments. The position provides broad exposure to frameworks such as SOC 2, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS, depending on business requirements. You will collaborate closely with Information Security, IT, Legal, Privacy, Internal Audit, and business stakeholders to translate security issues into actionable business risks. The role also involves third-party risk management, evidence collection, remediation tracking, and security reporting. This is an opportunity for a detail-oriented cybersecurity professional to strengthen security maturity while continuously improving GRC processes and automation.

Accountabilities

Perform cybersecurity and technology risk assessments across systems, applications, vendors, and business processes, documenting risks and evaluating their potential business impact.
Maintain information security policies, standards, procedures, control frameworks, risk registers, and governance documentation.
Support compliance activities aligned with frameworks and regulations such as SOC 2, HIPAA, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and other applicable requirements.
Assist with internal and external audits, regulatory examinations, security assessments, and customer compliance reviews by gathering, validating, and maintaining control evidence.
Track audit findings, security risks, control deficiencies, exceptions, and remediation plans through resolution, working with control owners to assess effectiveness and implement improvements.
Conduct third-party and vendor security assessments, including reviewing security questionnaires, certifications, audit reports, and supporting documentation.
Support security awareness, policy acknowledgment, risk acceptance, and security exception processes while responding to customer and partner due diligence requests.
Monitor changes in regulatory requirements, security standards, and cybersecurity practices and help translate relevant developments into governance improvements.
Develop GRC metrics, dashboards, reports, and management documentation to communicate security and compliance status effectively.
Partner with technical security teams to translate vulnerabilities and technical security issues into clear business risks and identify opportunities to automate and improve GRC processes.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Information Systems, Risk Management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
3+ years of experience in cybersecurity, governance, risk management, compliance, IT audit, or a related discipline.
Relevant certification such as Security+, CISA, CRISC, or CGRC is preferred.
Working knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks and standards such as HITRUST, SOC 2, PCI DSS, or comparable frameworks.
Experience performing security risk assessments and evaluating the effectiveness of security controls.
Familiarity with regulatory and compliance requirements relevant to technology-driven organizations.
Some experience or exposure to incident response, with a strong interest in cybersecurity and a willingness to continuously learn.
Strong analytical, organizational, planning, documentation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple assessments, findings, and deadlines.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain security, compliance, and risk concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Strong attention to detail, ability to meet deadlines, and proficiency with Microsoft Office or comparable productivity and reporting tools.
Curiosity about emerging technology and cybersecurity trends, with the ability to identify practical opportunities for improving security and IT infrastructure.

Benefits

Fully remote work arrangement in India.
Full-time opportunity within an Information Technology and cybersecurity environment.
Exposure to enterprise-wide cybersecurity governance, risk, compliance, and audit activities.
Hands-on experience with recognized security frameworks including SOC 2, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS.
Opportunity to work cross-functionally with Information Security, IT, Legal, Privacy, Internal Audit, and business teams.
Broad experience in third-party risk management, security assessments, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance.

Introduction

When you join the Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS), you join a team of more than 5,000 employees across the state dedicated to positively changing the lives of more than 1 million Marylanders each year. We do this by providing economic support, preventive services, and caring for children and adults.

We aim to deliver services so that we more quickly meet the needs of the people we serve. At DHS, we grapple with hard questions to find new ways to foster a culture of bold innovation. We do this to ensure that in Maryland, we leave no one behind.

GRADE

20

LOCATION OF POSITION

Maryland Department of Human Services

Division of Administrative Operations

S. Charles St.

Baltimore, MD 21201

Main Purpose of Job

The Deputy Director of the Office of Emergency Operations directs and coordinates the Department's emergency preparation, response and recovery operations statewide as mandated by the State Emergency Operations Plan (SEOP), both during steady-state and emergency operations. The position establishes statewide emergency operations plans and policies and oversees the implementation of such plans and policies at DHS Central and at the LDSSs as required by local plans and directives. This position manages 9 staff positions permanently assigned to the Office of Emergency Operations, and supervises additional staff assigned to emergency operations during an emergency event.

POSITION DUTIES

Develop, implement and administrate the federal, state and local emergency response plans and systems for DHS's Central office and the 24 local Departments of Social Services.
Coordinate, review, and update the mandated Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) for DHS and the local departments to ensure the readiness of all relocation and command center sites, communication devices, and support equipment as certified by the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM).
Develop hazard plans, conduct risk and vulnerability assessments, and coordinate training and preparedness initiatives to mitigate potential emergencies.
Direct and manage the implementation of the State Administrative Plan (SAP) for Individual Assistance (IA) in coordination with the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDE.M) and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).
Communicate with all levels of management concerning the preparations and response to emergency situations.
Communicate and coordinate with facility managers and contractors to ensure back-up power capacity and costs associated with back-up power provisions for communication and operation of State shelters during an emergency incident.
Coordinate and/or attend meetings, briefings, conferences, and seminars sponsored by federal, State, and local emergency management agencies as well as partner organizations and outside experts in the field.
Train the emergency operations coordinators throughout the department.
Facilitate meetings of federal, State and local emergency management agencies and other partner agencies, e.g. American Red Cross, for the purpose of ensuring the availability of resources for mass care, sheltering, and emergency assistance for the citizens and visitors of Maryland as a result of a natural or man-made disaster.
Manage State Shelter Containers (FEMA Shelter Containers were transferred from MDEM to DHS).
Oversee the maintenance of State shelter information database. The database is to be reviewed and updated annually.
Conduct annual updates of the local shelter supplies, etc., working in conjunction with the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the local school superintendents.
Conduct annual State shelter site visits to ensure the continued viability of the facility to be utilized as a state shelter site during or after a natural or man-made disaster.

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.

Experience:
Five years of supervisory experience in disaster response, OSHA, CPR, shelter operations, emergency health services, armed forces, law enforcement, firefighting, or similar emergency response environments.

The ideal candidate will possess the following:

Three years of experience creating emergency response plans, SOPs, and emergency policies.
Three years of experience managing incident reporting, conducting workplace safety assessments, or coordinating emergency operations with local, state, or federal partners.
One year of experience using computer software such as Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Google Docs/Sheets to create reports, spreadsheets, or presentations. .

Position Specific Description

The CM Project Controls team plays a critical role in managing and coordinating financial, logistical, and vendor-related activities throughout fossil outages. This position ensures precise financial tracking, seamless communication with stakeholders and vendors, and comprehensive documentation. This team is essential to the financial planning, execution, and closure phases of outages, ensuring all aspects are handled efficiently, within budget, and in compliance with established standards. This role demands a high level of organization, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities under pressure.

Up to 10-25% travel is required for this position during the spring and fall outage seasons. This position is planned to be based out of the Port Everglades Plant located in Ft. Lauderdale, FL, but working from one of the other FPL Fossil Sites within Florida will be considered based on experience and capabilities of the candidate selected and requires hiring manager approval.

Pre-Outage Responsibilities:

Prepare accruals and cashflow projections.
Participate in pre-outage meetings to align with stakeholders.
Calculate and finalize labor estimates.
Verify material costs and overheads.
Initial communication with vendors to establish outage expectations.
Internal/external collaboration on contract terms and vendor approvals.

Outage Responsibilities:

Adjust and communicate errors on actuals.
Report cost status and manage accruals and cashflow. Monitor internal labor spend and create POs/change orders as needed.
Review forecast versus budget and track material usage.
Evaluate scope changes and monitor milestones.
Approve invoices and ensure vendor summaries/timesheets are submitted.

Post-Outage Responsibilities:

Manage post-outage accruals and cashflow.

Knowledge of procurement processes and vendor management best practices.

new_jobs.description:
About The Role

The Commercial Analytics & DS team is the analytical engine of Hinge Health's commercial business – the team that CS, Partnerships/HSO, and Commercial leadership rely on for the data, metrics, and strategic thinking that drive client retention, program growth, and commercial decision-making. We build the self-service analytics infrastructure, AI-powered workflows, and high-stakes deliverables that define how HH's commercial organization understands and acts on its data.

We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst to serve as the team's senior individual contributor, dedicated AI champion, and organizational thought partner. You will independently own the team's most complex and highest-stakes initiatives – from the CS KPI and partner reporting suite to the commercial dbt data layer to the team's AI and self-service portfolio – and serve as the go-to analytical authority for CS, Commercial, and Partnerships/HSO leadership. AI ownership is a primary mandate, not a side contribution: the foundations are real (a working AFTR workflow, a first-generation Data Discovery Agent, active AnswerBot development), and your job is to take those proof points from promising to compounding. You are technically deep in SQL, dbt, and cloud data platforms – and you use that depth in service of framing strategy and owning methodology, not just executing it. The team operates lean and moves fast. If the role you are imagining requires someone to write tickets and execute – this is not it.

What You'll Accomplish

Strategic Analytics & Commercial Leadership

Serve as the primary analytical thought partner to CS, Commercial, and Partnerships/HSO leadership – owning the framing, scoping, and delivery of high-impact analyses across client retention strategy, surgery intent analytics, program expansion, commercial performance, client health, and performance guarantee reporting
Own and maintain the CS KPI and Bowler reporting suite – the dashboards and metrics CS leadership depends on to track commercial performance
Lead multi-quarter analytical initiatives end-to-end with full autonomy; the team's P0 initiatives (Analytics OS, client hub, retention model) should not require the hiring manager to carry them
Navigate complex cross-functional dynamics: manage stakeholder relationships without authority, push back constructively when data is being misread, drive alignment on methodology even when it is inconvenient, and absorb organizational friction so the rest of the team can focus on the work

AI Leadership & Self-Service Analytics

Own the team's AI and self-service strategy as the dedicated AI champion for Commercial Analytics – the counterpart to the AI lead role on HH's product-side Data Science team, with equivalent mandate and accountability
Scale and compound the team's existing AI portfolio: the CSM AnswerBot (v2 rebuild in Claude, a recurring stakeholder ask with active external pressure on timelines); the Data Discovery Agent (DDA) (v1 is in production and demonstrates the concept works; v2 must reach the reliability and scale the organization needs); and AFTR (Add Field To Report) v2.0 (proven internally as a meaningful toil-reducer; v2.0's ambition is to surface it directly to stakeholders so they can extend their own reports without analyst involvement)
Drive the team's contribution to the Analytics OS – the long-term platform into which the AnswerBot, DDA, and AFTR are intended to be incorporated; own Commercial Analytics' roadmap within it and ensure the tools you are scaling are being built toward that destination from day one
Use AI-assisted tools (Claude Code, Cursor, and equivalents) actively and with genuine curiosity; bring a real appetite for agentic workflows, and contribute to Matik-powered reporting automation that reduces the team's dependency on manual, recurring analytical requests

Data Modeling & Commercial Infrastructure

Own and evolve the commercial dbt data layer and mesh architecture – keeping it clean, well-tested, and scalable
Drive CDM enhancements including program-specific modeling (migraines, WPH, GI) and user-level pain reporting updates tied to the NRS/VAS transition
Partner with analytics engineers and data engineers to ensure commercial data flows reliably from upstream services into reporting-ready tables; advocate for upstream instrumentation best practices with Engineering partners

Communication, Teaching & Team Elevation

Communicate complexity simply and without condescension – you can explain a data model architecture, a statistical methodology, or a pipeline failure to a CSM, a CS VP, and a data engineer, and the explanation lands differently each time because you know your audience
Uplevel team analytical capability through documentation, structured knowledge transfer, ad hoc coaching, and building shared practices
Mentor through design reviews, analytical critique, and real pairing – actively raising the bar for what good looks like

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field or equivalent professional experience
3+ years of experience as a data analyst with a demonstrated track record of owning complex, cross-functional analytical work in a commercial or product environment
Sufficient technical depth in SQL, Python, and cloud data platforms (Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, or equivalent) to shape data architecture decisions, scope data model work, and partner credibly with analytics engineers
Experience delivering strategic analytical work to VP+ stakeholders – including framing ambiguous problems, developing methodology under uncertainty, and presenting results to people who will challenge you
Demonstrated ability to drive organizational alignment on data definitions, methodology, or reporting strategy across CS, Product, and engineering stakeholders without relying on formal authority
Deep healthcare industry knowledge – clinical, payer, provider, or digital health; the team's work (concurrent care, clinical outcomes, commercial contracting, payer reporting) demands fluency that only comes from having worked in it

Preferred Qualifications

Experience serving as a dedicated AI champion on an analytics team – not just a power user or early adopter, but someone who has taken existing AI proof points and scaled them into reliable, compounding capabilities that other people depend on; the portfolio here exists and is working – it needs ownership at scale
Track record of communicating analytical complexity to non-technical stakeholders clearly and without jargon – a CFO, a CSM team, and a data engineering team can all understand the same decision and walk away able to act on it
Prior experience building or leading self-service analytics platforms – including the governance, documentation, and training that makes self-service actually work; experience with a unified analytics platform that consolidates multiple tools under a shared architecture
History of mentoring analysts and raising team capability through shared standards, design review, and direct coaching – not just completing deliverables
Background in a lean, high-ownership team where you had to set your own analytical agenda rather than receive it – and a demonstrated preference for operating that way

Location & Hybrid Working Model — San Francisco

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ and follows Hinge Health’s hybrid working model. We believe that remote work and in-person work each have their own advantages, and we want to leverage the best of both worlds. Employees in hybrid roles are required to be in the office 3 days per week, for the full 8 hours of a typical business day. Our San Francisco office also has a dog-friendly workplace program.

About Hinge Health

Hinge Health leverages software, including AI, to largely automate care for joint and muscle health, delivering an outstanding member experience, improved member outcomes, and cost reductions for its clients. The company has designed its platform to address a broad spectrum of MSK care—from acute injury, to chronic pain, to post-surgical rehabilitation—and the platform can help to ease members’ pain, improve their function, and reduce their need for surgeries, all while driving health equity by allowing members to engage in their exercise therapy sessions from anywhere. The company is headquartered in San Francisco, California.

Learn more at http://www.hingehealth.com

What You'll Love About Us

Participation in our Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), allowing you to acquire company stock via payroll at a 15% discount against the lower market price.
Comprehensive and inclusive medical coverage and benefit programs for you and your dependents.
Flexible retirement savings through Traditional or Roth 401(k) investment paths.
Dedicated lifestyle stipends designed to fuel your professional growth and continuous learning.

Culture and Engagement

We make employment decisions without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, veteran status, disability status, pregnancy, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. If you feel you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, let us know by reaching out to your recruiter. If you receive a suspicious offer, stop communication and report it to the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center. new_jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Payments
new_jobs.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

Airbnb’s mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. As we grow to achieve that mission, we’re looking to add a technical, hands-on, and mission-driven Technical Program Manager (TPM) for the Payments team.

A person in this role will partner with our Payments organization to provide a cohesive set of technology offerings that enable everything related to moving money in Airbnb’s global marketplace - moving billions of dollars, in 191 countries, across 75 currencies, through a complex ecosystem of payments partners. Within Payments Tech, we have Payments Platform, Compliance & Operations, Payments Engineering Services, and Payments Data Engineering. These programs work together to deliver reliable systems that allow guests and Hosts to make and receive payments with clarity and ease. As our payments platform grows we’ll be adding new payment partners, global licenses, compliance and regulation controls, and building new payment experiences for our guests and hosts.

This role is deeply cross-organization, as projects will span across a wide surface area, and building positive relationships across a multitude of technical teams will be essential to the success of this leader. We are looking for candidates who share our passion for tackling complexity head-on while supporting and growing a world class team of Technical Program Managers. In addition to helping their team deliver predictable, consistent program execution, this leader should have a strong sense of ownership and ability to think and work strategically with a variety of stakeholders.

The Difference You Will Make

TPMs at Airbnb work on a variety of complex projects/ programs that touch multiple services, functions and teams, and hence are required to keep the big picture in focus while being

able to dive into the details, working through unique challenges we face daily. They're good at building relationships, motivating others with vision, and persuading with data. It is a highly leveraged role that aims to improve the quality and velocity of work across cross-functional teams by acting as a “force multiplier”. This includes managing project schedules, identifying risks, discussing the technical trade-offs with engineers, and maintaining clear communications across multiple stakeholder groups across the organization. In short, they get things done by bringing clarity out of chaos, diving into the details, and communicating clearly and in a timely manner.

A Typical Day

Develop program scope and objectives, collaborate with all relevant stakeholders, ensure technical feasibility and drive projects end-to-end.
Align on staffing, priorities and technical dependencies within Hosting and cross-functional teams like Trust, Payments, Infra & Product both in terms of quarterly planning, and managing ongoing risk escalation/ mitigation.
Manage Technical Design diligence process for large programs, track technical dependencies, scheduling reviews and pre-reviews, engaging the right stakeholders across teams, and managing meeting quality and efficiency.
Manage effective communications to leadership and across teams on key decisions, status, and risks to ensure accountability and timeline management.
Understand best practices, drive for process improvements, and find new ways of operating, with a focus on simplification and productivity.
Drive org-wide and company-wide technical initiatives as we evolve our technical stack to scale for the next decade
Provide visibility into key performance indicators so leaders are aware of risks and opportunities.

Your Expertise

Experience developing processes where few exist, and demonstrated flexibility to get things done.
Demonstrated ability to work through ambiguity to detailed solutions. You can take a vague problem, crisply frame the challenge, identify a path forward, and drive an initiative over the finish-line.
Good understanding of software engineers principles & proven ability to work in a distributed architecture environment.
Self-motivated, proactive and proven ability to adapt well and work with teams having different operating cadences.
Detail-oriented and able to understand the bigger picture by using your technical expertise and problem solving abilities to prioritize and manage blocking issues.
Experience working in a highly cross-functional environment where communication with multiple groups is imperative.
Ability to ramp up quickly and learn new technologies with minimal lag time.
Excellent written and oral business communication and people skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders.
Exhibit knowledge of Jira or other equivalent task management tooling.
BA/BS degree, 7+ years experience in software development industry

Your Location:

This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list. If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from.

Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging

new_jobs.title: Project Manager (IPT)
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Solar PV Project Manager is responsible for the full lifecycle of commercial and utility-scale solar construction projects—from early-stage diligence, planning and preconstruction through execution, commissioning, and closeout. This role integrates strategic planning, diligence, permitting, budgeting, and stakeholder coordination to ensure high quality projects are delivered safely, on time, and within budget. The Project Manager serves as the central point of accountability across engineering, development, construction, and finance teams.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Preconstruction Planning & Coordination
Lead preconstruction efforts from concept through mobilization.
Conduct constructability reviews, feasibility assessments, and site evaluations.
Conduct site visits during project diligence phase.
Coordinate topographical surveys, geotechnical investigations, and site access.
Develop scopes, timelines, and deliverables in collaboration with engineering, permitting, and development teams.
Organize and manage RFI and Value Engineering logs, and Risk logs.
Document meetings with developers, contractors, and internal stakeholders.

Construction Oversight
Manage multiple solar construction projects at various stages.
Oversee EPC relationships, qualifications, and contractor selection.
Conduct site visits for initial construction and QA/QC during buildout.
Ensure compliance with SSI technical specifications and local standards.
Maintain construction phase safety and Prevailing Wage and Apprenticeship compliance.

Documentation & Reporting
Maintain logs for drawings, submittals, RFIs, COs, PCOs, and deficiencies.
Prepare and manage meeting minutes and project updates.
Organize and maintain commercial project folders in SharePoint and Procore.
Prepare construction kick-off documentation including staging plans, safety plans, and quality plans.
Support all documentation requests from Structured Finance

Stakeholder Communication
Run internal Integrated Project Team meetings and external contractor calls.
Serve as the primary point of contact for internal teams, contractors, and external partners.
Provide regular updates to senior leadership and development partners.
Maintain accurate up to date information in ERP and CRM databases. Namely, schedule milestones, contractor information, budget and cost to date data.

Budgeting & Estimating
Prepare detailed CAPEX budgets.
Engage in value engineering efforts to optimize cost without compromising quality.
Manage RFPs for subcontractors and third-party engineering scopes, including bid leveling and scope gap analysis.
Develop initial construction schedules and cash flow projections.

Contract Management
Engage turn-key EPC partners and key subcontractors.
Develop detailed Scope of Work exhibit for each agreement, tailored to the project.
Prepare all EPC contract exhibits and lead negotiation of technical and commercial terms while coordinating with the Team Lead, General Manager and inside counsel.
Manage all EPC and subcontract agreements.
Review, document and process change orders.

Permitting & Regulatory Compliance
Contract and manage third party civil engineers in development of permit matrices for each project.
Oversee local, state, and federal permitting processes executed by EPC partners and subcontractors.
Ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations.

Design & Engineering Support
Interface with internal and external engineers to review system designs.
Ensure constructability and value engineering are integrated into design.
Support utility upgrade construction coordination as well as witness test scheduling.

Scheduling & Execution Strategy
Maintain project schedules using look-ahead planning and Critical Path Method.
Identify and mitigate schedule risks and delays.
Plan and monitor major material deliveries to avoid disruptions.
Confirm feasibility of sequencing, logistics, and mobilization plans.

Quality Assurance & Closeout
Develop and manage project quality control programs.
Oversee commissioning, punch-list resolution, and warranty follow-ups.
Prepare closeout documentation including O&M manuals.
Coordinate hand-off meetings with asset management.

Process Improvement & Standardization
Analyze and update SOPs for preconstruction and construction workflows.
Ensure compliance with internal stage-gate and project handoff procedures.
Promote continuous improvement across estimating, engineering, and transaction functions.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, Engineering, Renewable Energy, or related field.
5+ years of experience in solar PV project management or preconstruction.
Strong understanding of permitting, interconnection, site development, and EPC processes.
Proficiency in project management tools (e.g., Procore, NetSuite, Salesforce, MS Project, Bluebeam).
Excellent communication, negotiation, and leadership skills.
PMP or equivalent certification preferred.
NABCEP PVIP certification preferred, required within 2 years of hire.

Work Environment

This job operates in a fully in-person work environment, five days per week at our Rockville, MD headquarters, with office and field/site visits.
Ability to travel to project sites (local and out-of-state).
Must be able to walk and navigate uneven terrain during site visits.
May require PPE on active construction sites.
Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:
This is a full-time in-person position, and hours of work and days are typically Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Travel:
This position will travel to local solar installations and job sites to conduct tours with potential customers and others.

Physical Demands
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms. Physical working conditions may also involve the following:
Lifting up to 50 pounds.
Extended periods of sitting, walking, standing, reaching and/or bending.
Extended periods of reading fine print on a computer or in paper-based format.

.

Business Analyst

Job Description

HITT is seeking a Business Analyst to join the team designing and building HITT’s proprietary project software platform. This platform will support critical business capabilities across pricing, budgeting, financial management, and related processes.

This is a hands-on role for a meticulous, business-focused BA who can translate business needs into clear requirements and help drive solutions from concept through delivery. The successful candidate will work directly in the system, gather requirements, support QA and testing, clear blockers to keep development, builds, and releases moving, and flex into project management responsibilities as needed — including driving test cycles, tracking timelines, and coordinating dependencies.

The platform will continue to evolve, but the mandate is clear: deliver a pricing and financial management platform that elevates the business of building.
Reporting to Product Leadership, this role will partner closely with business stakeholders, field users, Product, Engineering, and System Integrator partners to translate high-value business problems into actionable requirements, and to deliver practical, intuitive solutions through rapid, iterative Agile cycles.

Because HITT builds software for builders, everything this role delivers must earn adoption in high-velocity, decentralized field environments—on jobsites, in trailers, and in offices—by users of many backgrounds. The specific components and feature-sets will evolve as HITT’s business and technology evolve; this role’s charge is durable: understand the business problem deeply, translate it clearly, and help the team keep shipping and raising the standard for what the platform can do.

Responsibilities

Discovery & Requirements

Lead requirements-gathering sessions, including workshops, interviews, and process walkthroughs.
Translate business needs into clear requirements, user stories, functional specifications, and acceptance criteria for the delivery team.
Partner with stakeholders to understand current-state ("as-is") processes, identify gaps, and define future-state ("to-be") solutions.
Perform fit-gap analysis against existing platform functionality and recommend build-vs.-configuration approaches and process/system improvements.
Identify risks, dependencies, and blockers, and work with the appropriate teams to resolve them.
Ensure requirements are clearly documented, understood, and communicated across business and technology teams.

Testing & Release Management

Develop test scenarios and scripts; support system, integration, regression, and User Acceptance Testing (UAT).
Lead or coordinate UAT activities and ensure solutions meet defined business requirements.
Triage and document defects, partner with technology teams on resolution, and validate fixes.
Support data mapping, validation, reconciliation, and migration activities as needed.
Support release planning, cutover, implementation, and post-go-live (hypercare) activities.
Track timelines, milestones, dependencies, and action items across multiple delivery teams.
Coordinate requirements gathering, UAT, and timelines across multiple concurrent System Integrator (SI) delivery partners, managing handoffs and dependencies between teams.
Help clear blockers and keep development and release activities moving forward.

Stakeholder Engagement & Ongoing Optimization

Build strong relationships with business stakeholders and end users, including frontline and field teams.
Spend time understanding how work is performed in practice, and translate those insights into better system solutions.
Maintain clear, current process documentation, functional requirements, training materials, and standard operating procedures.
Communicate status, risks, decisions, and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Support user training and adoption efforts, and incorporate user feedback into the product backlog.
Monitor system usage and user feedback to identify opportunities to improve system functionality, business processes, and user experience.
Contribute to product team standards, processes, and best practices for business analysis and delivery.
Stay current on platform capabilities, releases, and relevant industry practices.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field; equivalent experience considered.
5+ years of Business Analyst experience supporting enterprise software, technology, or business transformation initiatives.
Strong experience gathering and translating business requirements into actionable solutions and supporting the end-to-end delivery lifecycle.
Experience with QA/UAT, testing, defect resolution, and implementation.
Strong business process analysis, stakeholder management, and communication skills.
Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively across business and technology teams in an Agile or hybrid environment.
Construction management or other project-based/field-oriented industry experience preferred.

V-ZUG Business Controlling

Im Business Controlling von V-ZUG sind wir mehr als Zahlenmenschen, wir sind strategische Sparringspartner:innen, Impulsgeber:innen und Mitgestalter:innen der Zukunft. Mit einem tiefen Verständnis für unser Business und einem klaren Blick auf das grosse Ganze verbinden wir operative Exzellenz mit langfristiger Perspektive. Wir schaffen Transparenz, ermöglichen fundierte Entscheidungen und tragen aktiv dazu bei, dass V-ZUG als Premium-Marke nachhaltig wachsen kann – datenbasiert, vorausschauend und im engen Dialog mit unseren internen Partnern.

Das bietet dir die Stelle

Du konzipierst, entwickelst und betreust steuerungsrelevante Berichte, Dashboards und Analysen in Power BI und anderen Reportingtools eigenständig, damit Kennzahlen verständlich, transparent und entscheidungsrelevant werden
Du analysierst gemeinsam mit dem Data Analyst die Anforderungen und Entscheidungsbedürfnisse im Business Controlling und schaffst damit die Grundlage für wirkungsvolle Steuerungsinstrumente
Du nimmst Anforderungen unserer Stakeholder auf, strukturierst sie und übersetzt sie in klare fachliche Konzepte, Datenanforderungen und umsetzbare Lösungen
Du koordinierst und integrierst Reporting- und Controlling-Anforderungen aus den Fachbereichen und sorgst für ein konsistentes Gesamtbild
Du stellst ein einheitliches fachliches Verständnis von KPIs, Datenlogiken und Steuerungsmechanismen sicher und machst Entscheidungsgrundlagen nachvollziehbar
Du begleitest die Einführung und Weiterentwicklung von CO-Tools als fachlicher Power User und zentrale Schnittstelle zu digitalen Teams
Du dokumentierst Prozesse, Anforderungen, Entscheidungslogiken und KPI-Definitionen gemeinsam mit dem Data Analyst – strukturiert, verständlich und mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch
Du erkennst Verbesserungspotenziale in Reporting-, Analyse- und Controlling-Prozessen und treibst deren Umsetzung gemeinsam mit den relevanten Stakeholdern proaktiv voran

Das bringst du für die Stelle mit

Du hast eine Weiterbildung oder ein Studium in Betriebswirtschaft, Controlling, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder einem vergleichbaren Bereich abgeschlossen
Power BI gehört für dich zum Handwerk: Du verfügst über fundierte Kenntnisse in der Erstellung von Berichten, Dashboards und Analysen bis hin zur Anwendung von DAX
Du bringst einige Jahre Berufserfahrung im Controlling, Reporting, Business Intelligence oder in einer vergleichbaren analytischen Funktion mit
Du erkennst Zusammenhänge, leitest aus Daten fundierte Erkenntnisse ab und bringst auch komplexe Themen für unterschiedliche Anspruchsgruppen verständlich auf den Punkt. Dabei agierst du als geschätzte:r Sparringspartner:in und kommunizierst souverän auf Augenhöhe mit verschiedenen Stakeholdern.
Du begeisterst dich für digitale Systeme, moderne Tools und unsere interne AI. Du erkennst deren Potenzial und bringst neue Impulse für die Weiterentwicklung des Controllings ein
Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse – schriftlich wie mündlich – gehören bei dir zum Standard

Noch nicht überzeugt? V-ZUG bietet dir mehr als nur einen Job

Als Teil der V-ZUG Familie profitierst du von zeitgemässen Anstellungsbedingungen, vielfältigen Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten, geeigneter Infrastruktur sowie zahlreichen Angeboten und Dienstleistungen für dein persönliches Wohlbefinden.

Du arbeitest dort, wo die Perfektion unserer Produkte tagtäglich spürbar ist – von der Produktentwicklung über die Produktion bis hin zum Vertrieb. Zudem profitierst du von der direkten Verkehrsanbindung für Bus, Bahn und Auto, einem Mobilitätsbeitrag und vergünstigten Parkplätzen. Auch das Vergnügen kommt nicht zu kurz: So geniesst du im eigenen Personalrestaurant ausgewogene Menüs oder entspannst bei einer Massage im Sitzen, beides zu vergünstigten Preisen.

Wir fördern dein Wohlbefinden und deinen optimalen Ausgleich zwischen Arbeit und Freizeit. Innerhalb regulatorischer Rahmenbedingungen und entsprechend den Anforderungen der Arbeitsaufgaben hast du als Mitarbeiter:in der V-ZUG grösstmögliche Flexibilität. Egal, ob im Teilzeitmodell, Homeoffice oder Jobsharing – du arbeitest wann, wo und wie du am produktivsten bist.

Deine individuelle Entwicklung ist uns wichtig. Wir helfen dir dabei, deine Karriere durch kontinuierliche Aus- und Weiterbildungen, inspirierende Mentorinnen und Mentoren und eine Vielzahl an geeigneten Lernressourcen zu perfektionieren. Weiter bestehen zahlreiche Aktivitäten für ein unfallfreies und gesundes Arbeitsumfeld. So bleibst du als Profi rundum fit – heute und morgen.

Wir leben durchs Band den Grundsatz der Gleichstellung. Neben einer marktgerechten und fairen Entlöhnung trumpfen wir mit überdurchschnittlichen Sozialleistungen. Da wir auf einen Koordinationsabzug verzichten, profitieren auch Mitarbeitende mit Teilzeitarbeit von unserer Vorsorgelösung.

Eine weitere Selbstverständlichkeit ist für uns die vergünstigte Abgabe von V-ZUG Produkten an dich und deine Familienangehörigen.

Ausserdem stehen dir für deinen aktiven Ausgleich zur Arbeit vielfältige und attraktive Freizeitangebote zur Verfügung, bei welchen du von mehreren Vergünstigungen profitierst.

Als Arbeitgeberin schaffen wir eine wertschätzende Arbeitskultur, welche Neugier, neue Herangehensweisen sowie fachliche und persönliche Entwicklung durch das Erlernen neuer Kompetenzen fördert. Bei V-ZUG hast du die Möglichkeit, die Zukunft eines traditionsreichen Unternehmens voranzutreiben. Wir unterstützen dich dabei, dein volles Potenzial zu entfalten. Gemeinsam leisten wir täglich einen Beitrag für unsere Vision „Wir bringen Leichtigkeit in Ihr Zuhause und Kreativität in Ihre Küche“. Darauf sind wir stolz.

Wir stehen für eine bunte V-ZUG ein, indem wir Rahmenbedingungen schaffen, um von der existierenden Diversität im Unternehmen gegenseitig profitieren zu können. Was uns alle verbindet, ist der Teamgeist und die Passion für die Marke V-ZUG. Wir arbeiten eng und kollaborativ zusammen, vertrauen uns gegenseitig und begegnen unseren Mitmenschen mit Respekt und Interesse. Wir akzeptieren keinerlei Diskriminierung und sind überzeugt: Inklusion und Diversität machen unser Unternehmen stark und attraktiv. Jeder Einzelne und jede Einzelne trägt dazu bei, das „wir“ voranzubringen.

Als Arbeitgeberin verstehen wir es als Pflicht, die Mitarbeitenden für die Nachhaltigkeit zu sensibilisieren. So lancierten wir unter anderem ein Training zum Thema „Nachhaltigkeit und Ressourcenknappheit“ und starteten die V-ACT Challenge, bei welcher wir auf spielerische und aktivierende Art etwas Gutes für die Umwelt tun konnten. Darüber hinaus wurden sogenannte Awareness-Ambassadors in den Teams ernannt, welche monatliche Schwerpunktthemen vermitteln. Solche Initiativen sind nicht zuletzt eine hervorragende Gelegenheit für unsere Mitarbeitenden, eigene Anregungen für mehr Nachhaltigkeit bei V-ZUG einzubringen.

Join our innovative Analytics team and help enable a world-class Marketing organization. As a Staff Marketing Data Analyst, you will serve as the dedicated analytics partner to Marketing, using data, measurement, and experimentation to improve customer acquisition, marketing efficiency, and business growth. You will independently own complex analyses and measurement frameworks, translate data into actionable recommendations, and help Marketing leaders understand what is working, why it is working, and where to invest next. The successful candidate will combine deep marketing analytics expertise, analytical rigor, and strong business judgment with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive decisions without direct people-management responsibility.

What You'll Do

Partner cross-functionally with Marketing, Product, and other teams to improve marketing data quality, align data requirements, and ensure measurement approaches are consistent and trusted.
Independently lead actionable insights and deep-dive analyses that optimize customer acquisition, channel performance, campaign effectiveness, and marketing investment.
Own and advance multi-touch attribution (MTA), marketing mix modeling (MMM), and other measurement approaches to evaluate ROI across paid media, organic, and other marketing channels.
Design and scale experimentation approaches, including A/B testing and incrementality studies, to evaluate campaign effectiveness and inform investment decisions.
Define, monitor, and interpret core marketing KPIs, including customer acquisition cost (CAC), lifetime value (LTV), and campaign ROI, to assess marketing efficiency and growth performance.
Serve as a strategic thought partner to Marketing leaders, challenging assumptions and translating complex analytical findings into clear recommendations and business actions.
Raise the analytical bar across the team by sharing best practices, improving measurement standards, and coaching peers on marketing analytics methods and decision-making.

Requirements

7+ years of experience in marketing analytics, growth analytics, data analytics, or a related quantitative field, with demonstrated ownership of complex analytical work.
Master's degree in Analytics, Marketing, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a similar quantitative field.
Advanced SQL skills and proficiency in Python or a similar analytical programming language.
Experience with BI and data visualization tools such as Sigma, Tableau, Looker or similar platforms.
Deep understanding of marketing data, measurement, experimentation, and performance analysis, with demonstrated ability to independently translate insights into business action.
Experience with paid media and acquisition channels, including channel performance metrics and measurement approaches.
Hands-on knowledge of mobile app marketing analytics and MMPs, with AppsFlyer and SSOT experience strongly preferred.
Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence senior Marketing partners and drive decisions through data without formal authority.
Familiarity with modern data platforms and analytics workflows, such as Snowflake, AWS, dbt, or similar technologies.

Benefits And Perks

Our goal is to provide a comprehensive offering of benefits and perks that promote better financial, mental, and physical wellness.

We believe working alongside each other in person is the best way to build a great product and foster a strong company culture. Our expectation is that employees are in the office five days a week, allowing for optimal collaboration, inclusivity, and productivity. At the same time, we understand that life happens and recognize the importance of flexibility. We are committed to supporting our employees when circumstances arise that require remote work or adjusted schedules. Our goal is to ensure everyone can effectively balance personal and professional responsibilities while maintaining our collaborative and productive environment.

Here are some highlights of our benefits and perks offerings, feel free to ask your recruiting partner for more details on our comprehensive offering for employees.

100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents on your first day of employment.
Receive up to $100 per month in fitness reimbursement or enjoy a complimentary full membership to LifeTime Fitness or Equinox.
401(k) with a 3.5% match and immediate vesting
Meal program available for both lunch and dinner
Pre-tax benefits, including a $1,000 HSA match
Life and accidental insurance
Flexible PTO

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation and rewards package at Credit Genie. You may also be eligible to participate in the bonus and equity programs. You will also have access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, a 401(k) retirement plan with company match, short & long term disability insurance, life insurance, and flexible PTO along with many other benefits and perks.

Credit Genie is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer where we welcome and celebrate differences. We are committed to providing a workspace that is safe and inclusive, where everyone feels supported, connected, and inspired to do their best work. If you require any accommodations to participate in our recruitment process, please inform us of your needs when we contact you to schedule an interview.

new_jobs.title: IT Business Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Location:
Hybrid/Primary location at Stanford Campus in Palo Alto. Occasional travel between Stanford Campus in Palo Alto and Stanford Redwood City.

If you are a proactive, organized, and ServiceNow-savvy Asset Management Analyst looking to impact a dynamic organization significantly, we encourage you to apply. Join our team and help us optimize asset management processes to support our service growth and success.

The primary mission of the Stanford University Hardware Program (SUHP) is to provide an asset management lifecycle service to the University that safeguards Stanford’s valuable hardware assets, mitigates the risks associated with fraud and loss, and optimizes our budgeting processes.

The SUHP team seeks a talented Asset Management Analyst with exceptional organizational skills and expertise in ServiceNow to join our dynamic team. You will play a pivotal role in ensuring the security, integrity, and chain-of-custody for our hardware resources. Additionally, you will champion our environmentally responsible disposal practices while managing and optimizing our organization's assets and asset records, ensuring compliance with policies and regulations, and leveraging ServiceNow to streamline asset management processes.

The expected pay range for this position is $80,000 - $100,000
per annum.

Key Responsibilities

Asset Inventory Management, Tracking and Compliance:

Maintain a comprehensive workstation hardware and peripherals inventory through the ServiceNow Asset Management module. Ensure accurate asset records are maintained.
Conduct regular audits and assessments to track asset lifecycles, utilization, and depreciation.
Adhere to and enforce asset management policies and procedures to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry best practices.
Asset Disposition: Coordinate the disposal or surplus of assets following Stanford policies and Stanford’s Property Management Office (PMO)
Conduct monthly inventory counts with the team to reconcile against the expected stock.
Collaborate with vendors to negotiate favorable pricing for asset purchases.
Stay abreast of vendor hardware lifecycles.

ServiceNow/Data Analysis And Reporting Expertise

Collaborate and coordinate with ServiceNow administrators to customize and optimize asset management modules.
Utilize ServiceNow to automate asset management workflows, track asset requests, and streamline asset procurement processes.
Analyze asset data to identify trends, cost-saving opportunities, and areas for improvement.
Generate regular reports and dashboards to provide insights into asset utilization and performance.

Documentation Management And Collaboration

Maintain accurate documentation related to asset management processes and procedures.
Keep records of asset configurations, maintenance schedules, and procurement documentation.
Collaborate with Local IT, finance, procurement, and other departments to ensure seamless asset management across the organization.

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Analyze and document user needs, existing and new policies, processes, procedures and operational methods to consider possible improvements to new and existing systems.
Utilize elicitation techniques to understand business processes and translate into system requirements and/or development of systems solutions.
Define and document business requirements and test cases for system developments. May include the writing of all or a portion of functional specifications.
Coordinate with business and technology teams, ascertaining system requirements, such as program functions, output requirements, input data acquisition, and system techniques and controls.
Problem solve in areas such as system design, input/output requirements and procedural flow between departments and/or business systems.
Perform testing of new systems, upgrades and patching of existing systems; may include developing test plans. Conduct and document results of testing.
May develop instructional materials, training and job aids.

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree and three years relevant experience or a combination of education and relevant experience.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of computer system capabilities, business processes and workflow.
Understanding of the software development life cycle.
Experience with enterprise applications and understanding of database driven applications.
Skill in conducting interviews.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, including the ability to bridge functional and technical resources by communicating effectively with individuals of varying systems expertise and business needs.
Listening, negotiation and conflict resolution skills.
Ability to maintain good customer relations with clients and external vendors and partners.

About Us

At Stanford, every employee plays a part in our mission for a better tomorrow—from researchers to operations and from food services to educators. Join our team to work towards a future you believe in.
